# LTP testcase audit

Generated 2026-10-19. LTP at `0908d5a4ad33 2026-10-08 openposix: timers/twoevtimers: Wait for both timer signals`. Reference kernel: Linux 7.3-rc7 at /usr/src/linux. Documentation baseline: Linux man-pages (git master), kernel source and Documentation/, POSIX.1-2024 for POSIX tests.

## Scope and method

Every `.c` and `.sh` source under `testcases/` was read in full (5036 files, read in 67 groups of neighbouring directories), and 774 of the resulting findings were then verified by running them (see Verification below), and 318 libc-dependent findings were cross-checked against a musl build of the same tree (phase 3). Each file received one primary category and a confidence. Tests that looked suspicious were checked against the kernel source, the man page or the POSIX text before being placed in an action category, and the evidence is quoted in each entry. Style, API age (old `test.h` API) and modernisation are out of scope unless they affect results. `lib/newlib_tests` (library self-tests) are not test cases and were not audited.

Confidence: **high** means the claim was verified against kernel source, man page or POSIX text and is cited; **medium** means strong reasoning from the test code with partial verification; **low** means a suspicion that needs a human check.

## Summary

Phase 2 verified 976 findings by running tests on two Fedora 44 hosts (24-CPU bare metal, kernel 7.2.9; 1-CPU KVM guest, kernel 7.2.10): **863 confirmed**, **5 refuted** (moved to OK or a lesser category), **61 revised**, 32 unchanged (no new evidence either way), 15 new findings discovered while verifying. Each verified entry carries a "Verification" line with the commands run and what was observed; categories and confidence below reflect the verified state, with the phase-1 value shown in brackets where it changed.

Phase 3 re-checked 318 findings whose argument depended on C-library behaviour, using LTP built against musl 1.2.5 beside the glibc 2.43 build on the same host and the glibc, musl and libtirpc sources: **120 confirmed**, **0 refuted**, **13 revised**, 132 unchanged, 53 new. These entries carry a second "Verification (phase 3 ...)" line; where phases disagree, phase 3 wins.

## How to read this report

Each test file received one primary category. The category sections below hold one subsection per
test, with the claim under test, the concrete problem, the evidence (test line, kernel line, man page
or POSIX sentence) and a suggested action. Tests classified OK are listed only in the appendix. Where
an auditor wrote one entry for a family of files that share a defect (for example the tpm-tools
suite, the v4l tests or a set of generated POSIX tests), the per-file subsection is short and points
at the grouped entry at the end of that category.

### Phases, hosts and the Verification lines

The audit ran in three phases and the entries name them:

- **Phase 1** is the reading pass: every source file read against the kernel source, the man pages
  and the POSIX text. It produced the category, the claim, the problem, the evidence and the action
  in each entry. Files were read in 67 groups of neighbouring directories.
- **Phase 2** re-examined 774 of those findings by running them on two disposable Fedora 44 hosts
  (section "Verification on real hosts"). The evidence names the hosts **HPE** (the 24-CPU
  bare-metal machine, kernel 7.2.9) and **VIRT** (the 1-CPU KVM guest, kernel 7.2.10).
- **Phase 3** rebuilt the tree against musl beside the glibc build and compared the two, with the
  libc sources at hand (section "Cross-check against a second C library").

A verified entry carries one **Verification** line per phase: the verdict (CONFIRMED, REVISED,
REFUTED, UNCHANGED or NEW, defined in the two phase sections), the methods used, and the evidence
with the commands run and what they printed. Method tags:

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| RUN | the test was run as installed |
| READ | the source was re-read, usually together with the kernel source or the man page |
| MUTATION | a copy of the test was changed so that the behaviour it claims to check is wrong, rebuilt and run |
| BUILD | something was compiled: the mutant, a fixed version, a probe, or the whole tree |
| REPEAT | the run was repeated; the count is given |
| STRESS | run under stress-ng load on every CPU plus I/O and memory workers |
| CONTAINER | run inside a container or private namespace, or as a non-root user |
| VIRT | also run on the 1-CPU guest |
| GIT | LTP git history consulted for the intent of the code |
| MUSL | run or built against the musl build |
| SRC | the behaviour was located in the glibc, musl or libtirpc source and cited with file and line |
| BULK | taken from the whole-suite runs under both libcs rather than from an individual run |

Verification was done in numbered passes. When a file was examined by more than one pass, the
evidence pieces are joined with `||` and each is prefixed with the pass that produced it and its
verdict, for example `[v03: CONFIRMED]` or `[m09: NEW]`. Passes `v00` to `v21` belong to phase 2:
`v00` is the build and runtest cross-reference that checked every "never built or never run"
claim, `v01` to `v21` are the per-finding passes on the two hosts. Passes `m01` to `m09` belong to
phase 3: `m01` to `m07` are the per-finding passes under both libcs, `m08` is the triage of every
open_posix result that differs between the glibc and musl runs, and `m09` is the triage of every
`syscalls` runtest entry that differs.

Entries that phase 2 or 3 added ("Found in phase N verification") show the verdict as, for
example, `NEW (WRONG, high)  [category before this check: OK/high]`, and quote the commands and
their output in "Ran" and "Observed" blocks. Commands named `ltprun`, `ltprun-glibc`, `ltprun-musl`,
`ltpstress`, `ltpstress-glibc`, `ltpstress-musl` and `ltprepeat` are small wrappers installed on the
hosts: they run one installed LTP binary from the glibc or the musl build with the LTP environment
set, under stress-ng load, or N times with a tally, and print its output and exit status. Paths
under `/root/ltp-build`, `/root/build`, `/root/ltp-musl`, `/root/src` and `/opt/ltp*` are the build
trees, library sources and install prefixes on the bare-metal host.

In the appendix every file line carries `[verified: V]` with its phase-2 verdict and `[musl: V]`
with its phase-3 verdict where it has one.

Suggested order of work, by value per unit of effort:

1. **Drop dead code.** A large share of OBSOLETE entries are sources that are never built or never
   run (not in any runtest file, not in a Makefile, or impossible to compile against any supported
   kernel). Removing them is low risk and shrinks the tree noticeably.
2. **Fix tests that cannot fail.** Most WRONG entries are verification bugs: the test runs, prints
   TPASS, and would do so even if the kernel were broken. These give false confidence and are usually
   one-line fixes once identified.
3. **Relax checks on undocumented or undefined behavior.** UNDOC and UNDEF entries are candidates for
   false failures on correct kernels or other libcs. The fix is normally to accept every documented
   outcome, to set up the case so only one error condition applies, or to drop the subcase.
4. **De-flake.** FRAGILE entries fail on correct systems because of sleeps, containers, filesystems,
   tunables or hardware. Fix with proper synchronisation or detection (TCONF).
5. **Then WEAK and DOCS.** Low verification value and inaccurate descriptions; cheap to fix, low
   urgency.

## Verification on real hosts (phase 2)

After the reading pass, 774 findings were re-examined by running things on two disposable Fedora 44
machines: a 24-CPU bare-metal host (kernel 7.2.9) and a 1-CPU KVM guest (kernel 7.2.10), both with
LTP built from this tree and installed. The set covered every WRONG and FRAGILE entry, every
medium- or low-confidence OBSOLETE, UNDOC, UNDEF and DOCS entry, and every low-confidence WEAK
entry. High-confidence WEAK entries are value judgements and were not re-run.

Methods, by category:

- **WRONG, "check cannot fail":** mutation. A copy of the test was changed so that the behavior it
  claims to verify is wrong (syscall skipped, result replaced, flag removed, child made to fail) and
  rebuilt; if the test still reported PASS the finding is confirmed. Where phase 1 proposed a fix,
  the pass also applied it in several cases and showed that the mutant then fails.
- **WRONG, "wrong expectation":** run as-is on both kernels; a FAIL for the stated reason confirms.
- **FRAGILE:** 5 plain and 5 stressed runs (stress-ng on every CPU plus io and vm) on the big host and
  3 or more on the 1-CPU guest, plus the specific condition the finding names where it could be
  created: a container or private namespace, a non-root user, a tmpfs, overlayfs, ext2, vfat or
  noexec TMPDIR, a changed sysctl, a low rlimit, a CPU quota, a locale, a stepped clock, an RTC offset.
- **OBSOLETE "never built / never run":** a full build with a cross-reference of every installed
  binary and script against every runtest file, scenario file and calling script; a module-enabled
  build against kernel-devel for the kernel-module claims.
- **UNDOC, UNDEF, DOCS, WEAK:** run once, LTP git history for the intent, and a fresh read of the man
  page or POSIX.1-2024 text.

Outcome for the 976 verification records (some findings were checked by two passes):

| Verdict | Count | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| CONFIRMED | 863 | finding right; confidence raised where the evidence allowed |
| REVISED | 61 | finding partly right: category, confidence or mechanism changed |
| REFUTED | 5 | finding wrong, moved to OK; listed in their own section |
| UNCHANGED | 32 | no new evidence either way (feature not present on these hosts, or race not reproduced) |
| NEW | 15 | problems found while verifying that phase 1 had not flagged |

Confidence moved up for 312 findings (231 medium to high, 61 low to medium, 20 low to high) and
down for 35, almost all FRAGILE races that did not reproduce in 16 to 900 runs although a delay
mutant shows the mechanism is real. Every verified entry carries a **Verification** line with the
commands and what was observed, and the phase-1 category or confidence in brackets where it changed.

What the refutations have in common: all five came from reasoning about library internals without
running them (the `SAFE_SHMCTL` macro resets the id after IPC_RMID; `strtok` with the stringified
delimiter `','` strips the quotes; sockfs does implement listxattr). Where phase 1 only read the
test and the kernel, it held up.

What could not be verified here and keeps its phase-1 confidence: cgroup v1 controllers (Fedora 44
has no cpuset v1 and cpu/memory are v2), multi-node NUMA, Intel PT, HWP, a real TPM, a pre-6.9 or
pre-6.0 kernel, and a few tests that would have needed a reboot or an unrecoverable sysctl.

## Cross-check against a second C library (phase 3)

Phase 2 showed where the audit was weakest: all five refutations were wrong about what glibc or a
library does, and about 170 findings still rested on an argument of the form "glibc does X here,
POSIX does not require it". To test those arguments instead of asserting them, LTP was built a
second time from the same checkout against musl 1.2.5 (Fedora's `musl-clang`, with the kernel UAPI
headers, `sys/queue.h` and a libtirpc 1.3.8 built into the musl sysroot) beside the glibc 2.43
build on the 24-CPU host, and the glibc, musl and libtirpc sources were unpacked next to them.

Three kinds of data came out of it:

- **Build differences.** Only 10 of 2863 LTP binaries and 12 of 1639 open_posix binaries do not
  build under musl. Each is a finding in itself: the cpuset tests need glibc's `fts.h`,
  `fmtmsg01` uses `addseverity()`, `timer_create01/03` reach into glibc's private
  `_sigev_un._tid`, `pthread_rwlock_rdlock/2-1,2-2` use `_NP` rwlock kinds behind a guard that
  tests the compiler rather than the libc, the prioceiling tests never check
  `_POSIX_THREAD_PRIO_PROTECT`, and `aio_h/4-1` hard-codes glibc's `lio_listio` prototype.
- **Per-finding runs.** Every libc-dependent finding (170 files, the per-finding passes m01 to m07) was run
  under both libcs, repeated where timing mattered, and the libc behaviour it cites was located in
  the glibc or musl source and quoted with file and line.
- **Whole-suite comparison.** The complete open_posix conformance and functional suites were run
  under both libcs (1732 and 1720 results; 129 differ), and the
  whole `syscalls` runtest file was run under musl with every non-PASS re-run under glibc
  (1552 tests, 191 non-PASS under musl, 52 of them PASS under
  glibc). Every difference was triaged into "musl limitation or bug, test is right", "artefact of
  the run" or "test fault that glibc hides" (passes m08 and m09, see "How to read this report").

Outcome for the 318 files checked in phase 3:

| Verdict | Count | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| CONFIRMED | 120 | finding right; musl behaves differently or the libc source confirms the mechanism |
| REVISED | 13 | finding partly right: the mechanism, the suggested fix or the category changed |
| REFUTED | 0 | finding wrong |
| UNCHANGED | 132 | both libcs agree and the finding rests on the POSIX text alone, or the difference is a musl bug |
| NEW | 53 | tests rated OK that only pass because of glibc behaviour |

Entries touched by phase 3 carry a second **Verification (phase 3 ...)** line; where phases
disagree, phase 3 wins because it had the sources.

What musl changed in the picture:

- **Undefined behaviour stopped being latent.** Six pthread tests that pass on glibc crash with
  SIGSEGV on musl, which deliberately traps on joining or detaching a non-joinable thread
  (`pthread_attr_setdetachstate/2-1`, `pthread_cancel/5-1`, `pthread_detach/1-1,4-1,4-2`,
  `pthread_join/6-2`). `pthread_setcanceltype/1-1` and `pthread_mutex_init/1-2` hang or fail because
  musl disables cancellation while a mutex lock waits; `pthread_rwlock_wrlock/3-1` deadlocks instead
  of returning EDEADLK. All were UNDEF already; they are now demonstrated rather than argued.
- **glibc's error mapping hides wrong expectations.** `sem_unlink/4-1,5-1` pass only because glibc
  turns every invalid name into ENOENT and prefixes names with `sem.`; `sem_open/5-1` returns success
  without testing anything on either libc; `aio_read/10-1`, `aio_write/8-1,9-2` and `aio_read/11-2`
  fail on musl because it reports EBADF synchronously and has no prioritized I/O, both allowed by
  POSIX; `gethostname02`, `pathconf01`, `sysconf01`, `getpagesize01`, `shmt09` and `sbrk01` encode
  glibc's wrappers (musl's `sbrk` refuses any non-zero increment by design).
- **Some suggested fixes were glibc-shaped too.** The proposed fixes for `sem_unlink/5-1`
  (require ENAMETOOLONG), `mq_open/speculative/2-2` (assert EINVAL for a leading slash) and
  `getaddrinfo_01` (one error code) would fail on musl; the entries now carry corrected actions.
- **The obsolescent XSI signal family is still shipped.** `sighold`, `sigignore`, `sigpause`,
  `sigrelse` and `sigset` were removed from POSIX.1-2024, but musl exports them without deprecation
  and glibc with a deprecation warning only; the action for those 17 tests is softened from "drop"
  to "drop, or keep as Issue 7 legacy coverage". `sigpause/4-1` is the one test in the family that
  catches a real libc defect: musl hangs where it should return EINVAL.
- **Some phase-1 explanations were wrong even though the verdict held.** `sigwaitinfo/6-1` passes on
  glibc because glibc's `sigtimedwait` wrapper rewrites SI_TKILL to SI_USER, not because `raise()`
  avoids `tgkill`; `pthread_detach/4-2` reports UNTESTED on glibc because `pthread_detach` returns
  0, not ESRCH "by luck"; the RPC broadcast failure comes from how both libcs' `getifaddrs` report
  an address without `brd`, so "glibc" became "the C library" in those entries.
- **The whole-suite diff found patterns the per-item reading had missed.** Six scheduling tests
  (`sched_setparam/20-1,21-1,21-2`, `sched_setscheduler/15-2,22-1,22-2`) leave their error path
  through `pthread_exit((void *)-1)` from the main thread, so the process exits 0 and the suite
  counts a PASS; none of the 38 `sched_*`/`fork` tests that use process scheduling checks
  `_POSIX_PRIORITY_SCHEDULING` or `sysconf(_SC_PRIORITY_SCHEDULING)` before relying on it, so on a
  libc that declines the option (musl returns ENOSYS by design) they report UNRESOLVED or FAIL
  instead of UNSUPPORTED; six `pthread_attr_*stack*` tests read the stack of a fresh attribute,
  which POSIX leaves unspecified (glibc returns 0, musl EINVAL); three `sched_setparam/25-*` tests
  `#error` when `_POSIX_SPORADIC_SERVER` is undefined although POSIX allows that; `aio_h/4-1` was
  changed in 2020 from the POSIX `lio_listio` prototype to glibc's; and `sigismember/5-1` and
  `pthread_attr_setschedpolicy/4-1` require an EINVAL that POSIX only says "may" happen.
- **The syscalls runtest file under musl** is covered by pass m09; 139 entries fail under both
  libcs in this environment for reasons phase 2 already recorded (single NUMA node, no kernel
  modules, swap on btrfs, kernel 7.2 drift) and were not re-examined.
- **musl bugs found on the way** (not findings against the tests, recorded in the evidence):
  `aio_cancel` deadlocks on an in-progress request, `sigpause` ignores an invalid signal,
  `lio_listio` stops at the first failed submit, `pthread_cond_broadcast` wakes strictly in wait
  order regardless of priority, and `sysconf(_SC_THREAD_PRIO_INHERIT)` is hard-coded to -1.

Limits of this cross-check: musl is a second data point, not an oracle. Where both libcs agree the
finding still rests on the POSIX or man-page text and its confidence was left alone; where musl
disagrees because it is non-conformant, the finding was not credited for it. The comparison covers
one architecture (x86_64) and one musl version.

## Recurring patterns

The same handful of root causes explain most of the findings. They are worth knowing because they
suggest tree-wide checks rather than one-off fixes.

**Verification that cannot fail.** Wrapper scripts that end with `exit 0` or whose last command is
`rm -rf` or `tst_resm TINFO` (test_controllers.sh, the cpuctl suite, sched_stress.sh, realtime
run.sh, fs_racer.sh, smt_smp_affinity.sh); parents that check `WEXITSTATUS()` without `WIFEXITED()`
so a child killed by a signal counts as PASS (open_posix sigaction 17-*, 22-*, 25-*, raise/1-2,
mq_notify 2-1 and 9-1); comparisons of a value with itself (the float_* suite, dup07, dup202,
getpagesize01, mv_tests backup check); `(flags & 0) != 0` style checks (socket02, socketpair02,
pipe2_01); results computed and never asserted (mq_notify01, pth_str03, pi_perf, openposix
pthread_create/s-c1); inverted errno logic (aio_read/9-1, aio_write/7-1, mmap/27-1); copy-paste
leftovers (acct02 reads stime for utime, pthread_atfork/1-1 checks the parent twice,
pthread_mutex_setprioceiling/1-1 never calls setprioceiling, nftw test29A/30A call the ENOTDIR
helper). A grep for `exit 0` at the end of runner scripts and for `WEXITSTATUS` without
`WIFEXITED` would find more of these.

**Regressions introduced by mechanical conversions.** Several WRONG entries were correct in the old
API and lost their check during the new-API conversion or a mass edit: mmap03 dropped its memcmp
(5c778f6cd65d), fchmod04 dropped seteuid(nobody) (7ede1cd15414), rename13 now renames a path onto
itself (f93f55eeb32f), recvmsg01 moved SCM_RIGHTS cases to PF_INET where TCP ignores them, munmap03
passes the address of a pointer variable (0c7346cb0974), fcntl33 lost the assignment that enables
its overlayfs exception, migrate_pages03 runs the migration as nobody (53eac722fd37), the IPv6
multicast query tests send queries from a non-link-local address the kernel drops (ef227aca9ef1),
if-addr-addlarge deletes each address right after adding it (f925eece9747). In the POSIX suite,
commit d3df7e05e9f7 ("Replace SIGPOLL with SIGUSR2") hand-edited generated sigaction files, turned
nine `-2.c` SIGALRM tests into byte-identical copies of the `-18.c` SIGUSR2 tests, and so removed
SIGALRM coverage from those families. Compiler optimisation is a related trap: work loops with no
side effects compile to nothing at -O2 (realtime tc-2 and periodic_cpu_load, open_posix
sched_setparam/2-1, 2-2, pthread_exit/6-2), so timing and CPU-accounting checks pass trivially.

**Kernel drift.** Tests whose premise the kernel has since removed or changed: /proc/schedstat
version 17 renamed the domain line (6.14), so every cpuset_sched_domains case fails; the pipe
user-pages soft limit is skipped for root (pipe15 passes without reaching the regression);
setsockopt08 (CVE-2021-22555) is rejected before the vulnerable path since 6.9; set_mempolicy05's
compat heuristic is invalid since the compat path was removed in 5.15; memcg charge moving was
removed in 6.13; DCCP in 6.16 and UDP-Lite in 7.1; sys_sysctl in 5.5; the powerpc endian switch in
6.12; mandatory locking in 5.15 (fcntl14, fcntl16, ftruncate04); tracing_enabled; the Blackfin
register table in ptrace04; statmount flag 1 and landlock flag 1 gained meanings in 7.0; v4l2 returns
ENOTTY not EINVAL since 3.1. The tbio, tpci-adjacent, v4l and usb kernel modules cannot compile
against any supported kernel and the build silently ignores that.

**Code that is never built or never run.** About a hundred rpc/rpc-tirpc variant clients
(`*_mt`, `*_stress`, `*_complex`, `*_dataint`, `*_limits`, `*_performance`, `*_scalability`),
open_posix stress/threads (no Makefile, never had one), v4l/user_space and usb, memtoy,
mmc_security, the sched_tc0..3 load generators, async_handler_tsc, gtod_infinite, setgroups04,
mmap-corruption01, shmat1, nfsv4/acl/acl1.c, ltpSockets, fs_racer_dir_test, cpuhotplug01 (commented
out), cmdlib.sh/net_cmdlib.sh. Separately, over a hundred open_posix `N-M.sh` scripts (plus their
build-time `<func>_N-M.sh` copies) only echo "Tested implicitly via assertion N" and exit 0, which
the runner records as PASS.

**Undocumented error precedence.** Many errno tests set up two error conditions at once and pass
only because of the order the kernel happens to check them: EROFS cases run as nobody on a root-owned
file (chown04, fchmod06, fchown04, fchownat03, lchown02, linkat02, utimes01 is the documented
exception), EINVAL-before-EBADF or -EFAULT with closed or NULL arguments (dup3_02, io_cancel01/02,
mq_notify02, prctl02, name_to_handle_at02, accept01), F_GETLK probes that overlap several locks
(fcntl11/19/20/21), the max_map_count off-by-one. The fix is to make each case trigger exactly one
documented error.

**POSIX-undefined behavior required by the conformance suite.** POSIX.1-2008 and 2024 removed many
"shall fail" errors that the 2002-era tests still demand: pthread_join/detach/cancel on an already
joined or detached thread, re-initialising or destroying a locked rwlock or mutex, spinlock EBUSY and
EDEADLK, invalid timer ids, uninitialised attribute objects, pthread_once with automatic storage.
Tests also count a POSIX-permitted spurious wakeup as FAIL (pthread_cond_wait/1-1,
pthread_cond_timedwait/1-1, 2-2), require "may fail" errors (getgroups01, fpathconf01,
sigaddset/4-1, aio EBADF synchronously) and require a single waiter for EPOLLEXCLUSIVE. These pass
on glibc and Linux today; the question for maintainers is whether to keep them as Linux behavior
tests (then document that) or drop them from a conformance suite.

**Environment assumptions.** sleep()-based handshakes (flock07, nanosleep02, kill02, semop05, the
open_posix mq_*, cond_* and cancel tests), privileges and containers (bind02 ignores
ip_unprivileged_port_start, memfd_create01 fails with memfd_noexec set, mlock/12-1 as a normal user,
17 mq tests create queues above msg_max as non-root, ptrace11 under Yama, sched_getscheduler/7-1 on
pid 1), filesystems (open12 on vfat, ustat01/02 on a btrfs root, hugemmap11 O_DIRECT on tmpfs,
fallocate03, name_to_handle_at on overlayfs, vma05 on distros with /lib64), hardware and latency
thresholds (the realtime suite, dctcp01, sctp01, timerfd01, epoll_wait04, getrusage04,
cpufreq_boost, irqbalance01), tunables (sysfs tests, membarrier01 under nohz_full,
overcommit_memory, min_free_kbytes).

**Side effects worth fixing regardless of category.** cpuhotplug07 runs `make mrproper` in
/usr/src/linux by default; block_dev tc07 taints the kernel with a WARN on every run and disables
later taint checks; tpci unbinds live PCI drivers; madvise01 uses MADV_HWPOISON as a smoke test and
poisons host pages; kvm_pagefault01 reloads kvm with npt/ept off and never restores it; tcp_cc_lib.sh
never restores tcp_congestion_control; mmap/24-1 lowers max_map_count and restores it only on
failure; tirpc_svc_tp_create registers a bogus RPC program and never unregisters it;
pthread_atfork/3-3 reaches about 1.9 GB RSS; the pthread_mutex_lock s-c tests exhaust thread and PID
limits; the tpm-tools suite is destructive and order-dependent; twopsetclock moves the wall clock.

**Man pages that disagree with the kernel.** In these cases the tests follow the kernel and were
left OK, but the man-pages project should be told: get_mempolicy with MPOL_F_ADDR and a NULL address
returns EFAULT (man says EINVAL); init_module with an unsigned module under enforcement returns
EKEYREJECTED (man says ENOKEY); getsockopt with a wrong level returns EOPNOTSUPP (not listed);
fsconfig with fd < 0 returns EINVAL (man says EBADF); Q_GETNEXTQUOTA with no next id returns ENOENT
(man says ESRCH); unshare can return EMFILE (not listed); epoll_ctl can return EFAULT (not listed).

### Patterns that only showed up when running

- **A child killed by its signal counts as PASS.** Many open_posix tests check `WEXITSTATUS()`
  without `WIFEXITED()`; when the child dies of the very signal under test the status reads 0 and the
  test passes. Mutation showed this for the whole sigaction 17-* and 22-* families and several
  sigqueue/sigpause tests, and it also hides signals that are ignored by default (SIGCHLD, SIGURG,
  SIGCONT).
- **The workload is optimized away.** In `periodic_cpu_load`, `tc-2` and `sched_setparam/2-1`, the
  installed binary's busy loop compiles to a bare `ret` or a single add, so timing-based verdicts
  measure nothing.
- **Hard-coded "nonexistent" pid 999999.** Both hosts set pid_max to 4194304 and the big host's pid
  counter crossed 999999 on its own during the session; inside a pid namespace where that pid is alive
  the sigqueue and kill tests fail.
- **Non-root runs report FAIL, not UNRESOLVED.** Sixteen mq_receive/mq_timedreceive tests, the
  priority tests and several others misreport a missing privilege as a conformance failure.
- **Side effects seen live:** `mmap/24-1` lowers vm.max_map_count on its normal pass path;
  `runpwtests03` leaves every CPU on the userspace governor; `tcp_cc_lib` leaves dctcp as the
  congestion control; `gethostid01` creates /etc/hostid; `rpc_test.sh` cannot kill servers whose
  name exceeds 15 characters; `tirpc_svc_tp_create` leaves an RPC program registered.
- **Vacuous per-filesystem coverage.** `open12` lacks `.mount_device`, so all ten "testing on <fs>"
  iterations run on the same TMPDIR; adding it makes vfat fail and exfat break, as phase 1 predicted.

## Caveats

The classification was produced by 67 model-driven reading passes over every source file, with
kernel source, man pages and POSIX consulted for anything flagged, followed by 22 verification
passes that ran the flagged tests, mutated copies of them and repeated runs under load on two
Fedora 44 hosts (kernels 7.2.9 and 7.2.10), and 9 cross-check passes against a musl build of the same
tree with the glibc, musl and libtirpc sources at hand. Findings that were in neither set (most OK
entries and high-confidence WEAK entries) rest on reading alone, except that every open_posix test and
every `syscalls` runtest entry was at least run once under both libcs and any difference triaged. Entries whose Verification line
says UNCHANGED kept their phase-1 confidence because the hosts could not exercise them. Negative
results for races ("not reproduced in N runs") do not prove absence; the entry says whether a delay
mutant showed the mechanism. Claims about libc or libtirpc internals in entries without a phase-3 line were made without the library
source; entries with one cite the file and line. The musl comparison covers one version (1.2.5) on x86_64.
POSIX judgements use the 2024 edition; where an older edition still listed an error the entry says
so. Numbers in the summary tables count primary categories only and reflect the verified state;
secondary tags appear in brackets in the appendix.


## WRONG: Incorrect expectation or ineffective check

The test asserts something the kernel source, man page or POSIX contradicts, or its verification is broken so it can pass without exercising the claimed behavior (wrong variable checked, unreachable failure path, child failure not propagated, result ignored). Results from these tests are misleading in one direction or the other. Action: fix the check, or drop the test or subcase if it cannot be fixed.

351 testcases. Sorted by path; confidence shown in each entry.

### testcases/kernel/containers/utsname/utsname04.c  (runtest: containers/utsname04_clone, utsname04_unshare)
- Category: WRONG
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: An unprivileged process gets EPERM from clone()/unshare() with CLONE_NEWUTS.
- Problem: The errno check is `TST_EXP_PASS(errno == EPERM)`. TST_EXP_PASS expands to TEST(SCALL),
  and TEST() does `errno = 0;` before evaluating SCALL, so the expression is always `0 == EPERM`
  -> 0, which TST_EXP_PASS reports as TPASS regardless of the real errno. (Had errno survived, the
  logic would also be inverted: a true comparison returns 1, which TST_EXP_PASS reports as
  "invalid retval".) Only "the call failed" is really verified; the errno is never checked. In
  the clone mode tst_res() calls also run between the failure and the check.
- Evidence: utsname04.c:42, 46; include/tst_test_macros.h:43-48 (TEST sets errno = 0) and 279-299
  (TST_EXP_PASS_SILENT_ treats non-zero as failure). clone(2)/unshare(2) document EPERM for
  CLONE_NEWUTS without CAP_SYS_ADMIN.
- Suggested action: Use TST_EXP_FAIL(unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS), EPERM) and, for clone, save errno
  right after tst_clone() and check it with TST_EXP_EQ_LI(saved_errno, EPERM).
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION. HPE as-is: clone/unshare modes TPASS 'errno == EPERM passed'. Mutated work copy so the call fails with EINVAL (clone flags CLONE_NEWUTS|CLONE_THREAD; unshare(-1)): both modes still 'TPASS: errno == EPERM passed' (passed 2 failed 0) -> errno check is vacuous (TEST() zeroes errno before evaluating errno == EPERM)

### testcases/kernel/controllers/cpuctl/run_cpuctl_latency_test.sh  (runtest: controllers/controllers via test_controllers.sh)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: OBSOLETE, FRAGILE)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: wakeup latency of a sleeping task stays below 2x the scheduler wakeup granularity with 100 CPU hogs, without (test 1) and with (test 2) cpu cgroups.
- Problem: the verdict never reaches the harness. cpuctl_latency_check_task exits 1 on FAIL, but the script only echoes "TBROK ..." and ends with `cd $PWD`, so it always exits 0. The parent test_controllers.sh also always ends with `exit 0`. The "sources compiled" check `[ ! -f $cpuctl_latency_test ]` uses undefined variables, so it collapses to `[ ! -f ]` and never fires. The threshold comes from /proc/sys/kernel/sched_wakeup_granularity_ns, which moved to debugfs in 5.13 and no longer exists under EEVDF. So the code always uses the (log2(ncpus)+1)*5ms*2 fallback, which the kernel does not promise for 100 runnable hogs at the same nice level. Test 2 depends on parameters.sh mounting a v1 hierarchy with only `cpu`. That fails with EBUSY on any host where cpu is co-mounted with cpuacct (kernel/cgroup/cgroup-v1.c:1214-1218 skips the mismatched root, then rebind_subsystems refuses a controller that is already bound). On v2 hosts the whole suite TCONFs in test_controllers.sh.
- Evidence: run_cpuctl_latency_test.sh:98-99, :129, final `wait $check_task` / `cd $PWD` block; test_controllers.sh:101 `exit 0`; no sched_wakeup_granularity sysctl in /usr/src/linux/kernel/sched/.
- Suggested action: drop. If kept, propagate the check task's exit status and rewrite it on the new shell API with a cgroup v2 path (tst_cgctl).
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: test 1 as-is PASS (max 3447us), script rc 0. Copy with allowed_latency=0: 'FAIL The Latency test 1 failed', 'Task exited abnormally with return value: 1', 'TBROK Test could'nt execute...' yet SCRIPT_RC=0. Test 2 (unshare -m): 'ERROR: Could not mount cgroup filesystem on /dev/cpuctl' (cpu bound to v2). Via test_controllers.sh: TCONF on any cgroup2 host

### testcases/kernel/controllers/cpuctl_fj/run_cpuctl_test_fj.sh  (runtest: controllers/controllers via test_controllers.sh)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: FRAGILE, OBSOLETE)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: 22 cases on v1 cpu.shares parsing and clamping, root restrictions, attach rules, and share-based CPU distribution.
- Problem: (1) case5 ("attach realtime process") writes PID 3 to tasks and requires EINVAL. That assumes PID 3 is an RT kthread (migration/0 on 2.6 kernels) and that CONFIG_RT_GROUP_SCHED is active. On current kernels PID 3 is the SCHED_NORMAL `pool_workqueue_release` kthread (kernel/workqueue.c:8253, the first kthread created in workqueue_init). It has no PF_NO_SETAFFINITY, so cgroup_procs_write_start (kernel/cgroup/cgroup.c:3150) accepts it and case5 FAILs on a correct kernel. RT tasks are only refused when rt_group_sched_enabled() (kernel/sched/core.c:9640-9650). (2) do_test prints TFAIL when cleanup fails and then TPASS for the same case (no `continue`). (3) Each case ends with `wait $pid`, and SIGUSR1 is sent right after spawning cpuctl_fj_cpu-hog. If the signal arrives before sigaction(), the default action kills the hog and wait returns 138, so the case fails. (4) case19-22 judge one `top -bn1` sample (line 8, column 9) against windows such as 96-103% or 44-56% on a shared CPU0, and case21/22 need all 10 samples in range. That depends on load, the top version and .toprc. (5) If the v1 `-o cpu` mount fails (cpu co-mounted with cpuacct), all 22 cases report TFAIL instead of TCONF. The script's exit status never reflects TFAIL, and the parent exits 0. The other EINVAL/clamp expectations (cases 6-17) match kernel/sched/fair.c:15720-15723 and kstrtoull parsing.
- Evidence: run_cpuctl_test_fj.sh:230-249, 284-292, 99, 600, 641, 674, 697-707, 51-55.
- Suggested action: drop case5 (or create an RT task, check CONFIG_RT_GROUP_SCHED and attach it). Fix the TPASS-after-TFAIL bug and TCONF on mount failure. Better: drop the suite in favor of cgroup v2 cpu.weight tests.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,READ. HPE: PID 3 = pool_workqueue_release, SCHED_OTHER, flags 0x208040 (no PF_NO_SETAFFINITY); cpuctl_fj_simple_echo 3 > <v2 cgroup>/cgroup.procs -> rc 0 (case5 needs 22) and PID 3 moved. Script as-is (unshare -m): 22x 'failed to mount cpu subsystem' + 22x 'caseN FAIL' (no TCONF), script rc 0. Early SIGUSR1 kills cpuctl_fj_cpu-hog (rc 138) 1/10 when sent at once

### testcases/kernel/controllers/cpuset/cpuset_hotplug_test/cpuset_hotplug_test.sh  (runtest: controllers/cpuset_hotplug)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: FRAGILE, DOCS)
- Confidence: medium
- Claim under test: offlining or onlining CPU1 updates root and child cpuset.cpus, and the affinity of tasks in the cpuset follows.
- Problem: in the root cases (1-2) and the "EMPTY" general case, the "task cpus" value is read from /sys/devices/system/cpu/present instead of the task's Cpus_allowed_list. The task's affinity is never checked, and the comparison against cpus_all (0..online_count-1) is unrelated to cpusets. It also fails falsely whenever present != online, for example with nosmt or maxcpus=, where online can be a contiguous 0-N (so ncpus_check passes) while present is larger. Hotplugging CPU1 is assumed to be possible: only Hyper-V is excluded, so a missing or refused cpu1/online gives TFAIL instead of TCONF. `sleep 1` waits for asynchronous task migration out of an emptied cpuset (cpuset_migrate_tasks_workfn, kernel/cgroup/cpuset-v1.c:270-321). This is acknowledged in the code with an issue link. TST_TOTAL=13 but only 6 cases run.
- Evidence: cpuset_hotplug_test.sh:96, :188, :26; cpuset_funcs.sh:130-135, 246-259.
- Suggested action: read /proc/$tst_pid/status Cpus_allowed_list in all cases and compare it with the online mask. TCONF if cpu1/online is missing or not writable. Fix TST_TOTAL.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **UNCHANGED** via RUN,READ. Cannot exercise: Fedora 44 kernels have CONFIG_CPUSETS_V1 unset, /proc/cgroups has no cpuset line -> HPE 'cpuset_hotplug 1 TCONF: Cpuset is not supported' (same on VIRT). Re-read confirms task_cpus read from /sys/devices/system/cpu/present (:96, :188), TST_TOTAL=13 with 6 cases, no TCONF for unwritable cpu1/online

### testcases/kernel/controllers/cpuset/cpuset_lib/cpuinfo.c  (runtest: helper library for controllers/cpuset_sched_domains)
- Category: WRONG
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: getcpuinfo()/get_sched_domains() reads each CPU's sched-domain span from
  /proc/schedstat so cpuset_sched_domains_check can compare it with the expected partition.
- Problem: The parser does `sscanf(buf, "%s %s", str1, str2)` and feeds the second token of
  every `domainN` line to bitmask_parsehex(). Since schedstat version 17 (kernel commit
  011b3a14dc66 "sched/stats: Print domain name in /proc/schedstat", v6.14) the line is
  `domainN <name> <cpumask> ...`, so str2 is "SMT"/"MC"/"PKG"/"NUMA". strtoul() reads no hex
  digits, bitmask_parsehex() returns error, get_sched_domains() returns -1, and getcpuinfo()
  fails. Every caller therefore fails on 6.14+ kernels. The format is documented and versioned
  ("version N" header line), so the parser should check the version or skip the name field.
- Evidence: cpuinfo.c:222 (sscanf "%s %s"), cpuinfo.c:239 (bitmask_parsehex(str2)), cpuinfo.c:279;
  libbitmask.c:241-246 (nchars_read < 1 -> err); /usr/src/linux/kernel/sched/stats.c:107
  (SCHEDSTAT_VERSION 17) and :139 `seq_printf(seq, "domain%d %s %*pb", dcount++, sd->name, ...)`;
  Documentation/scheduler/sched-stats.rst:8-9 "The domain field prints the name of the
  corresponding sched domain from this version onwards" and :91 `domain<N> <name> <cpumask> ...`.
- Suggested action: Read the "version" line; for version >= 17 parse the third token
  (`sscanf(buf, "%s %*s %s", ...)`), else the second.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION,BUILD. HPE /proc/schedstat 'version 17', lines 'domain0 SMT 001001 ...'. Original cpuset_sched_domains_check: 'get sched domain's info for each cpu failed' -> 'TFAIL: getcpuinfo failed'. Rebuilt with cpuinfo.c parsing the 3rd token for domain lines: getcpuinfo succeeds and the check proceeds to partition_domains (fails there only because cpuset v1 is not built in)

### testcases/kernel/controllers/cpuset/cpuset_load_balance_test/cpuset_sched_domains_check.c  (runtest: helper run by controllers/cpuset_sched_domains)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: FRAGILE)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: The sched domain span of every CPU matches the partition that cpuset
  sched_load_balance settings should produce.
- Problem: It calls getcpuinfo() (cpuset_lib/cpuinfo.c) and reports TFAIL when that fails.
  On kernels >= 6.14 getcpuinfo() always fails because of the schedstat v17 domain-name
  field (see cpuinfo.c entry), so the check always reports "getcpuinfo failed" without
  testing anything. Secondary: /proc/schedstat exists only with CONFIG_SCHEDSTATS
  (kernel/sched/build_utility.c:73), and a missing file gives TFAIL instead of TCONF. The
  expected partition also ignores CPUs removed from load balancing by isolcpus=domain /
  nohz_full (housekeeping HK_TYPE_DOMAIN), so such systems mismatch.
- Evidence: cpuset_sched_domains_check.c:66-67; cpuinfo.c:217-218 (fopen fail -> -1);
  kernel/sched/stats.c:139.
- Suggested action: Fix the parser in cpuinfo.c. Return TCONF when /proc/schedstat is
  missing. Exclude non-housekeeping CPUs from the expected domains, or TCONF when
  isolcpus is set.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION,BUILD. HPE (kernel 7.2.9, schedstat v17): ltprun cpuset_sched_domains_check -> 'cpuset_sched_domains_check.c:67: getcpuinfo failed' RC=1 before any domain comparison; same binary with fixed cpuinfo.c parser gets past getcpuinfo (fails later at :72 partition domains only because CPUSETS_V1=n)

### testcases/kernel/controllers/cpuset/cpuset_load_balance_test/cpuset_sched_domains_test.sh  (runtest: controllers/cpuset_sched_domains)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: FRAGILE)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: cpuset sched_load_balance / cpus / CPU hotplug combinations partition
  the scheduler domains correctly (19 cases).
- Problem: Each case decides pass/fail only through the exit status of
  cpuset_sched_domains_check. That helper fails unconditionally on 6.14+ because of the
  schedstat domain-name field, so all 19 cases TFAIL on current kernels whatever the
  partitioning is. Secondary: it waits for domain rebuild with a fixed `sleep 1` before
  checking, and does not handle isolcpus/nohz_full or !CONFIG_SCHEDSTATS.
- Evidence: cpuset_sched_domains_test.sh:77-78, 120-121, 196-197 (sleep 1 +
  cpuset_sched_domains_check); cpuinfo.c:222/239; kernel/sched/stats.c:139.
- Suggested action: Fix cpuinfo.c parsing (see above), then add a TCONF for missing
  /proc/schedstat and isolated CPUs.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION. HPE/VIRT as-is: 'cpuset_sched_domains 1 TCONF: Cpuset is not supported' (CONFIG_CPUSETS_V1 unset, 1 node). Each case's verdict = exit status of cpuset_sched_domains_check, which was shown to TFAIL 'getcpuinfo failed' on the schedstat v17 format here, so on any >=6.14 host with cpuset v1 every case fails regardless of partitioning

### testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/fork_freeze.sh  (runtest: via test_controllers.sh -> run_freezer.sh)
- Category: WRONG
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: freezing a cgroup while a forkbomb (timed_forkbomb) runs inside it.
- Problem: timed_forkbomb is started in the background by a non-interactive bash, so its stdin is /dev/null (POSIX async-list rule, verified). The `echo go >> /proc/$pid/fd/0` on line 45 writes to /dev/null. timed_forkbomb.c:58 `while (scanf("%as", &word) < 1) {}` then spins forever on EOF (-1). Even with real input it would spin, because with LTP's -std=gnu99 glibc uses the C99 scanf, where "%a" is a float conversion, so "go" returns 0 (verified by compiling a test). No fork ever happens; the test freezes and thaws one busy-looping task. Line 29 also sources ${CGROUPS_TESTROOT}/libltp, which is not in INSTALL_TARGETS.
- Evidence: fork_freeze.sh:38-55; timed_forkbomb.c:56-61; include/mk/config.mk:67 (-std=gnu99); freezer/Makefile INSTALL_TARGETS.
- Suggested action: start the helper with a pipe or FIFO as stdin and use `%ms` (or just a pipe/signal handshake) in timed_forkbomb.c, or drop it in favour of the cgroup_fj freezer stress tests.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,READ. HPE (v1 freezer): fork_freeze.sh RC 0 ('line 29: .../libltp: No such file or directory'); during the run ps shows exactly 1 timed_forkbomb, state R ~48% CPU, /proc/PID/fd/0 -> /dev/null -> the 'echo go' goes to /dev/null, the helper spins in scanf and never forks; the test freezes/thaws one busy loop and passes
- Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): **CONFIRMED** via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: fork_freeze.sh RC=0, 1 timed_forkbomb state R 49% CPU, fd0->/dev/null; musl: RC=0, 1 timed_forkbomb (ld-musl) R 42%, fd0->/dev/null. Probe sscanf("go","%as")=0, sscanf("")=-1 under both (glibc binary imports __isoc99_scanf; musl vfscanf.c:301 'a' is a float conv) -> helper spins in scanf under either libc, never forks

### testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/freeze_move_thaw.sh  (runtest: via test_controllers.sh -> run_freezer.sh)
- Category: WRONG
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: moving a task out of a FROZEN cgroup into a THAWED cgroup fails, and the task stays frozen in the original group.
- Problem: The kernel has allowed migrating frozen tasks for a long time. freezer_attach() thaws a task that moves into a non-freezing cgroup, and the v1 freezer has no can_attach. The write to child2/tasks therefore succeeds, which sets result=1 (line 57). The task is then thawed and in child2, so assert_sample_proc_is_frozen at line 71 fails. The test always fails on current kernels. run_freezer.sh stops at the first failure, so this also stops freeze_cancel, freeze_self_thaw, stop_* and fork_freeze from running. The script's own comments (lines 24-28, 63-94) expected that the semantics might go this way and say how to flip the asserts.
- Evidence: freeze_move_thaw.sh:56-73; kernel/cgroup/legacy_freezer.c:144-185 ("Tasks can be migrated into a different freezer anytime regardless of its current state ... !(freezer->state & CGROUP_FREEZING) -> __thaw_task(task)").
- Suggested action: change to the documented semantics: the move succeeds, the task is in child2 and not frozen. Drop the stale comments.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN. HPE (v1 freezer, 7.2.9): 'freeze_move_thaw.sh 1 TFAIL : Expected task 1062575 to be frozen (unexpected task state: "S")' RC 1 -> the move into the THAWED cgroup succeeded and thawed the task, as kernel/cgroup/legacy_freezer.c freezer_attach() documents; run_freezer.sh stops here, so later scripts never run

### testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/freeze_self_thaw.sh  (runtest: via test_controllers.sh -> run_freezer.sh)
- Category: WRONG
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: a task in a cgroup freezes its own cgroup by writing FROZEN, and the test then thaws it.
- Problem: In sleep_freeze_self_sleep() (line 40) the background subshell does `export sample_proc=$!`. Inside an async subshell `$!` is not the subshell's own PID: it is empty here, because no earlier background job exists (checked: `( echo $! ) &` prints empty). add_sample_proc_to_cgroup therefore reports a TFAIL and writes an empty string to tasks (EINVAL). The subshell never joins the cgroup, so it freezes an empty cgroup and keeps running. In the parent, sample_proc is the subshell PID, which is in state S, so assert_sample_proc_is_frozen (line 66) fails. Self-freezing is never exercised. Today this is hidden only because run_freezer.sh stops at freeze_move_thaw.sh first.
- Evidence: freeze_self_thaw.sh:38-49,64-66; libcgroup_freezer add_sample_proc_to_named_cgroup / assert_task_is_frozen.
- Suggested action: use `$BASHPID` (or `sh -c 'echo $$ > tasks; ...'`) inside the subshell.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,READ. HPE: 'TFAIL : Expected pid  does not exist', 'echo: write error: Invalid argument', 'TFAIL : Failed to add sample process  to cgroup', 'TINFO :    freezing itself' (empty pid), 'TFAIL : Expected task N to be frozen (unexpected task state: "S")' RC 1. bash -c '( echo $! ) & wait' prints empty

### testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/freeze_write_freezing.sh  (runtest: via test_controllers.sh -> run_freezer.sh)
- Category: WRONG
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: writing "FREEZING" to a FROZEN cgroup fails with EIO and the state stays FROZEN.
- Problem: It has the same broken `> freezer.state 2>&1 | grep 'Input/output error$'` construct (line 44) as write_freezing.sh. grep never matches, the ERR trap breaks out before the line-46 assert, and the script exits 0. The kernel returns EINVAL, not EIO.
- Evidence: freeze_write_freezing.sh:44-47,60; kernel/cgroup/legacy_freezer.c:410-428.
- Suggested action: the same fix as write_freezing.sh.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION,VIRT. HPE as-is RC 0. Mutated copy writing THAWED instead of FREEZING to the FROZEN cgroup (state really changes) still RC 0 on HPE and VIRT -> the 'state stays FROZEN' assert is never reached. Direct check: FREEZING written to a FROZEN v1 freezer -> 'write error: Invalid argument', state FROZEN (EINVAL, not EIO)

### testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/run_freezer.sh  (runtest: via test_controllers.sh)
- Category: WRONG (phase 1: WEAK)
- Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
- Claim under test: driver that runs all v1 freezer scripts.

### testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/timed_forkbomb.c  (helper for fork_freeze.sh)
- Category: WRONG
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: helper that waits for a word on stdin, then fork-bombs for N seconds.
- Problem: `while (scanf("%as", &word) < 1)` never terminates. Under -std=gnu99, "%a" is the C99 float conversion (returns 0 on "go" and leaves the input unconsumed), and on EOF it returns -1. It also passes char** to a float conversion (UB). See fork_freeze.sh.
- Evidence: timed_forkbomb.c:56-61.
- Suggested action: use `%ms`, or a simple read() on a pipe/FIFO; treat EOF as "go" or as an error.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,BUILD. Local: scanf("%as") built with -std=gnu99 (and default gnu17): 'echo go |' -> ret=0 three times (input not consumed), '</dev/null' -> ret=-1; so 'while (scanf(...) < 1)' never ends. HPE: the helper started by fork_freeze.sh stays a single R-state process for the whole test (no fork)

  check compr_data_size < orig_data_size from mm_stat, or reword the description.

- Verification conclusion: Since the library started reporting kernel ntfs3 as a separate filesystem, zram01 fails on any system with ntfs3 and mkfs.ntfs. zram_makefs() calls `mkfs.$fs` directly, and mkfs.ntfs3 does not exist. ### testcases/kernel/fs/doio/growfiles.c  (runtest: fs/gf01..gf30, fs_readonly/test_robind01..30, scsi_debug.part1)

A failed write in -w mode therefore produces TPASS. Runtest entries using -w: gf01, gf14, gf18, gf27, gf28 (and the matching test_robind/scsi_debug entries). Also: cleanup() loops `ind <= num_files` and unlinks filenames + num_files*PATH_MAX, which is one slot past the malloc(num_files*PATH_MAX) buffer (heap out-of-bounds read; it unlinks a garbage path). With -q r (not used in runtest) check_write() leaves ret = bytes read (>= 0) and reports a false "CW" mismatch with an uninitialized errmsg, because the PATTERN_RANDOM branch is an empty statement.
- Evidence: growfiles.c:2042-2056 (the -w write path has no `return -1` after `if (ret != 1)`); growfiles.c:2530-2542 (`fsize <= Woffset` returns 0, "no validation, but not an error"); growfiles.c:1795 (`for (ind = 0; ind <= num_files; ind++) unlink(...)`) vs growfiles.c malloc(num_files * PATH_MAX); growfiles.c:2651 (empty PATTERN_RANDOM branch, then `if (ret >= 0)` reports corruption).
- Suggested action: add `return -1;` (after unlocking) for every failed write in the -w branch, as the normal write branch does; change the cleanup loop to `ind < num_files`; skip check_write when Pattern == PATTERN_RANDOM.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: gf01 (-w mode) TPASS as-is. Mutation: the 1-byte -w write_buffer() gets fd -1 (EBADF on every write) -> gf01 still 'TPASS: Test passed' rc=0 over its 20s run: failed non-ENOSPC writes in -w mode are never errors. cleanup() OOB unlink not checked (no ASAN/valgrind on hosts)

### testcases/kernel/fs/fsx-linux/fsx-linux.c  (runtest: ltp-aiodio.part3/fsx01..fsx10; also net.nfs fsx.sh)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: WEAK, DOCS)

  whatever the kernel returned, hiding any corruption from later op_read() checks.
  (2) The `-o` "Maximum size for single operation" option is parsed into op_max_size but
  op_max_size is never used; operation sizes are drawn from the whole file_max_size range.
  runtest fsx05..fsx10 (`-N 10000 -o 1024..32768`) therefore all run the same workload as fsx04.
  (3) Help text says `-l` is "Maximum size in MB" but tst_parse_filesize() takes bytes
  (runtest `-l 500000` = ~500 KB); `-w/-r/-t` are byte alignments, not "page alignment".
- Evidence: fsx-linux.c:222-228 (memcpy then memory_compare of the same bytes);
  `grep op_max_size` shows only lines 40,48,326,327,371 (declaration/parse/help, no use);
  op_file_position() calls at 132,164,188,209,247 use file_size/file_max_size only.
- Suggested action: in op_map_read compare `addr` to `file_buff + pos.offset` without the
  memcpy; clamp pos.size to op_max_size in op_file_position(); fix the option help strings.
  Otherwise drop fsx05..fsx10 as duplicates.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: fsx01 TPASS as-is. Mutation: pwrite 'Z' into the file at the map-read offset (model untouched) right before mmap -> 'TPASS: All file operations succeed' (-N 2000); same plus memcpy removed -> TFAIL. fsx-linux -N 2000 -o 1024 -D: 1571/1601 ops had size>1024, max 255783 -> -o ignored

### testcases/kernel/fs/ftest/ftest05.c  (runtest: fs/ftest05)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: WEAK)
- Confidence: high

Old-lib tst_exit() exits with T_exitval, which is 0 when no failure was reported, so the parent counts the child as passed and that child silently stops testing. On a correct kernel a below-EOF read always returns csize, so this branch exists only to catch a bug, and it hides it. The sibling ftest01.c (of which this is a copy) uses `tst_brkm(TFAIL, ...)` at the same spot. Apart from this the test duplicates ftest01: it only replaces lseek with lseek64, and with max_size = 1 MiB no offset ever needs 64 bits.
- Evidence: ftest05.c:350-354 (`if (xfr != csize) { /* tst_resm commented */ tst_exit(); }`); ftest01.c:356-361 (tst_brkm(TFAIL)); lib/tst_res.c:414-427 (tst_exit -> exit(T_exitval & ~TINFO)); ftest05.c:149 (max_size = K_1 * K_1).
- Suggested action: Replace the bare tst_exit() with tst_brkm(TFAIL, NULL, "xfr=%d != %d, zero read", ...) as in ftest01. Consider dropping ftest05 as a duplicate of ftest01, or making it use offsets above 2 GiB so lseek64 actually matters.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: ftest05 TPASS as-is. Mutation: in the 'below EOF, not seen yet' branch force xfr = csize - 1 (short read) -> every child hits the bare tst_exit() with T_exitval 0 and the run still reports 'TPASS: Test passed.' rc=0 -> a short read below EOF is silently ignored

### testcases/kernel/fs/openfile/openfile.c  (runtest: fs/openfile01)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: WEAK)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: "Create files and open simultaneously": N threads each fopen() the same file M times concurrently.
- Problem: No failure can produce a FAIL result. (1) If a thread's fopen() fails it only calls perror and pthread_exit() (lines 218-226). It never increments c.thr_sleeping, so main blocks forever in pthread_cond_wait at lines 161-162: a hang or timeout instead of TFAIL. (2) main never joins the threads. It prints TPASS "Threads are done reading" (line 185) right after the broadcast, while the threads have not yet closed their files, and then `_exit(0)`, so thread errors after wakeup are invisible. (3) Every TFAIL path in main calls cleanup(), which only does tst_rmdir() and returns (lines 64-68), so execution continues (e.g. with fd == NULL) and still reaches TPASS and `_exit(0)`. The exit status is therefore always 0. In the end the test checks only that fopen("rw") works 10x10 times, and reports even that wrongly.
- Evidence: openfile.c:64-68, 128-131, 161-168, 185-190, 218-226.
- Suggested action: Convert to the new API. Have threads return status, join them in main and TFAIL on any open failure, increment the counter (or use a barrier) even on error, and use tst_brk instead of falling through. Alternatively drop it: the open() limit/concurrency coverage exists in syscalls/open*, and fs_fill/stress tests cover the rest.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: openfile -f10 -t10 with stdout to a file: rc=0 and 0 bytes of output (TPASS line lost, _exit(0) skips stdio flush). Mutation thread 0 fopen fails -> 10x 'FAIL - Couldn't open file' then hang until timeout rc=124. Mutation TFAIL+cleanup() before TPASS in main -> rc=0, 0 bytes output: failures in main cannot fail the test

### testcases/kernel/hotplug/cpu_hotplug/functional/cpuhotplug07.sh  (runtest: cpuhotplug/cpuhotplug07)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: FRAGILE, WEAK)
- Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
- Claim under test: offlining a CPU while a kernel compile is running migrates the compile process off that CPU.
- Problem: `KCOMPILE_LOOP_PID` is the `cpuhotplug_do_kcompile_loop` wrapper shell, which spends its time blocked in wait() for `make`; the make/cc children were forked before `set_affinity` and keep their original mask, so the compile load is never pinned to the CPU being offlined. For a sleeping task, `sched_setaffinity` does not move it (affine_move_task only acts on running/queued tasks), and CPU offline only pushes runnable tasks, so `ps -o psr` (task_cpu) of the sleeping shell just reports its last CPU: the check passes trivially when that CPU was not CPU_TO_TEST, and can falsely TFAIL when it was. Environment: the loop runs `make mrproper` in the -d dir (default runtest arg /usr/src/linux), destroying the user's kernel config/build tree; `bzImage` target exists only on x86/arm/s390/m68k/parisc, so on arm64/ppc64 there is no compile load; cleanup kills only the shell with SIGKILL, leaving the running make tree orphaned.
- Evidence: cpuhotplug07.sh:88-113; tools/cpuhotplug_do_kcompile_loop:17-20; include/cpuhotplug_hotplug.sh:52-58; /usr/src/linux/kernel/sched/core.c affine_move_task() (~2969: only task_on_cpu/TASK_WAKING/task_on_rq_queued paths migrate); runtest/cpuhotplug:9 `-d /usr/src/linux`.

### testcases/kernel/io/ltp-aiodio/aio-stress.c  (runtest: ltp-aio-stress/ADS1000-ADS1053+)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: WEAK, FRAGILE)
- Confidence: high

(2) Every runtest entry passes exactly one `-oN`; for `-o1` (read) and `-o3` (random read) the only stage run is a read of the freshly created, empty fileN.bin in TMPDIR, so every read returns 0 bytes and `st_size > offset + res` is false, so it is not counted as an error. These entries (ADS1005-1012, 1018-1025, 1031-1053, ...) pass without reading any data. (3) `-o0` is meant to add the write stage, but `if (stages_i)` skips 0, so `-o0` silently falls back to "all stages". (4) With the default `-a 500` iterations and 1 GB file size, record sizes <= 256k never finish the write stage, so read/verify stages are never reached anyway. (5) `-v` verification mismatches are printed as TINFO and never fail. (6) Default 1 GB per file x up to 8 files with no free-space check; ENOSPC is then ignored per (1). Also: `stages_i` is uninitialised when -o is omitted; `-m` is declared without ':' so it always TBROKs; SAFE_SHMGET result is not stored in shm_id.
- Evidence: aio-stress.c:324-358 (check_finished_io), :1205-1208 (stages_i), :1283-1290 (first_stage), :1060-1063 & :1117-1118 (iterations loop / restart), :1310-1318 (fresh files); runtest/ltp-aio-stress.
- Suggested action: count any `res != buf_size` on writes as an error; turn verify mismatches into failures; always run a write stage (or pre-fill files) before read-only stages and fix `-o0`; reduce default -s or check free space; otherwise drop the read-only runtest variants.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,READ. HPE: ADS1000/ADS1005 TPASS. On a 4 MiB tmpfs TMPDIR, 'aio-stress -o2 -r4k -f1 -s 64m' (random writes far past ENOSPC) -> TPASS, no 'io err' line: write errors ignored. '-o1 -s 16m -v' reads a fresh empty file -> TPASS. '-o0' prints no 'Adding stage' (stage 0 skipped -> all stages). '-m' -> 'TBROK: Invalid shm option'. Also -s is bytes ('-s 64' TBROK too small), help says MB

### testcases/kernel/io/ltp-aiodio/aiodio_append.c  (runtest: ltp-aiodio.part4 AD000-AD009)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: DOCS)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: "Append zeroed data to a file using libaio [O_DIRECT] while other processes are doing buffered reads and check if the buffer reads always see zero" - i.e. a buffered reader at EOF must never see stale/uninitialised blocks while AIO DIO extends the file.
- Problem: the reader children run common.h `io_read_eof()`, which does `offset = SAFE_LSEEK(fd, SEEK_END, 0);`. SAFE_LSEEK's signature is `(fd, offset, whence)` (include/tst_safe_macros_inline.h:183), so this is `lseek(fd, 2, SEEK_SET)`: every iteration seeks to byte 2 and reads 4096 bytes from the *start* of the file. The readers therefore never touch the region being appended (after the first 64K write lands, bytes 2..4098 are stable zeros forever), and the test can only PASS. The claimed race (buffered read racing an O_DIRECT append past EOF) is never exercised. The bug predates the new-API conversion: the 2004 code already had `lseek(fd, SEEK_END, 0)` (git show 2283d3c0559b), so this test has been a no-op for its entire history. Secondary: `-n` help says "default 16", code default is 8 (line 32 vs 193).
- Evidence: testcases/kernel/io/ltp-aiodio/common.h:122; include/tst_safe_macros_inline.h:183-184; aiodio_append.c:148.
- Suggested action: change common.h:122 to `SAFE_LSEEK(fd, 0, SEEK_END)` (and consider reading a little before EOF, e.g. seek to max(0, size - bufsize), since a read exactly at EOF returns 0 bytes and checks nothing). Fix the `-n` help text.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: AD000 TPASS as-is (also VIRT). Mutation: every AIO append after the initial batch writes 0x41 instead of zeros -> still 'TPASS: All bytes read were zeroed'. Same + common.h io_read_eof seeking to EOF-4096 (SAFE_LSEEK(fd, 0, SEEK_END)) -> 'TFAIL: Non zero bytes read'. Readers never look near EOF

### testcases/kernel/io/ltp-aiodio/dio_append.c  (runtest: ltp-aiodio.part4 ADI000-ADI009)

Mutation: io_append() writes 0x41 for every block after the first -> 'dio_append -c 2000' still TPASS 'All bytes read were zeroed'; same + io_read_eof() seeking to EOF-4096 -> 'TFAIL: Non zero bytes read'. ### testcases/kernel/mem/shmt/shmt05.c  (runtest: mm/shmt05)
- Category: WRONG
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: "Create two shared memory segments and attach them ... The addresses DO BUMP into each other. The second attach should Fail."
- Problem: The second shmat() is shmat(shmid, cp + SHMSIZE/2, 0) with SHMSIZE=16, i.e. an address 8 bytes into an existing page and without SHM_RND. The kernel rejects it at the alignment check before ever checking for an overlapping mapping, so EINVAL would be returned even if the overlap check were missing. It also re-attaches the first segment (shmid); shmid1 is created and never attached (the old version used shmid1).
- Evidence: shmt05.c:34-35; ipc/shm.c:1542-1557 (`if (addr & (shmlba - 1)) ... if (addr & ~PAGE_MASK) goto out;` -> -EINVAL) precedes the overlap check at ipc/shm.c:1655-1661 (`find_vma_intersection(...)` -> -EINVAL). shmat(2): "EINVAL ... unaligned (i.e., not page-aligned and SHM_RND was not specified)" vs SHM_REMAP text "Normally, an EINVAL error would result if a mapping already exists in this address range."
- Suggested action: attach shmid1 at a page-aligned address inside the first attachment (e.g. cp itself, or cp + page with a multi-page first segment), or rename the test to "unaligned shmaddr -> EINVAL" (already covered by shmat02).
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: shmt05 TPASS EINVAL as-is. Mutation: shmdt(cp) before the 2nd shmat so nothing overlaps -> still 'TPASS: shmat(shmid, cp + 8, 0) : EINVAL' (alignment check). Control: shmat(shmid1, cp, 0) (aligned, overlapping) -> EINVAL from the overlap check. Test never exercises overlap

### testcases/kernel/mem/shmt/shmt09.c  (runtest: mm/shmt09)
- Category: WRONG
- Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
- Claim under test: "Attach at an address that is less than the break value: should FAIL."
- Problem: The heap is moved by +16384, -4097, +512 bytes, leaving the break 511 bytes past a page boundary (kernel stores the unaligned brk value; glibc malloc keeps its own brk page-aligned). vp = sbrk(0) - 32 is therefore not page aligned, and shmat() without SHM_RND fails with EINVAL at the alignment check, not because the address lies inside the heap VMA. The heap-overlap rule is never exercised. (The later SHM_RND attach above brk + sbrk() -> ENOMEM part is valid.) Side note: sbrk(-16000) shrinks 3201 bytes below the break the test started from, i.e. into glibc's own heap.
- Evidence: shmt09.c:47-60, :62; ipc/shm.c:1542-1557 vs :1655-1661.
- Suggested action: use a page-aligned address inside the heap (e.g. `(void *)((unsigned long)sbrk(0) & ~(SHMLBA - 1)) - SHMLBA` after growing brk by several pages) so the EINVAL comes from the overlap check.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: instrumented vp=0xeba31df page-offset=479 (unaligned; brk ends 0x...1ff as phase 1 said). Mutation: vp=0x200000000008 (unmapped, unaligned, far from heap) -> still TPASS EINVAL. Control: vp page-aligned inside heap -> EINVAL (overlap). The heap-overlap rule is never exercised; the SHM_RND/sbrk ENOMEM part passes
- Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): **NEW** (second finding, secondary category UNDEF/high; primary kept) via MUSL,RUN,SRC. [m01: UNCHANGED] HPE glibc: TPASS shmat EINVAL + TPASS sbrk ENOMEM; musl: 'shmt09.c:48: TFAIL: Error: sbrk failed, errno = 12' (separate problem, see NEW line). The unaligned-vp/EINVAL mechanism is kernel-side (ipc/shm.c) and libc-independent; phase-2 mutation stands || [m01: NEW] musl src/linux/sbrk.c:9 'if (inc) return ENOMEM' by design -> under musl shmt09 aborts with TFAIL at its first sbrk(16384) on a correct kernel, and the final TST_EXP_FAIL(sbrk(INCREMENT), ENOMEM) would pass vacuously. glibc misc/sbrk.c:74 moves the break. Use the raw brk syscall (tst_syscall(__NR_brk), as brk01/02) or TCONF when sbrk(n!=0) is unsupported
- Verification conclusion: The original finding (an unaligned vp, so the EINVAL comes from the alignment check, not from overlapping the heap) is kernel-side, and the phase-2 mutation stands. Under musl the test never gets that far (next section).

### testcases/kernel/sched/hyperthreading/ht_affinity/smt_smp_affinity.sh  (runtest: hyperthreading/smt_smp_affinity)

A TFAIL from ht_affinity is therefore never reflected in the exit code. Conversely, when CPUs are offline it prints TCONF but exits 1 (TFAILCNT incremented), i.e. reports a failure on a configuration it means to skip. `cpu_cores` from `grep "cpu cores" | ... | uniq` can be several lines on hybrid/heterogeneous systems, which breaks `[ $cpu_cores -ge 1 ]`, and the script then prints "TBD" and exits 0 without testing anything.
- Evidence: smt_smp_affinity.sh:31-35, 39-46, 47-59, 64.
- Suggested action: drop with ht_affinity, or propagate `./ht_affinity`'s exit status and exit 32 (TCONF) for the offline-CPU case.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: in a dir with the real ht_enabled and a fake ht_affinity that prints 'tst_resm TFAIL' and exits 1, smt_smp_affinity.sh prints 'TFAIL : MUT: fake ht_affinity failure' then 'End: SMT/SMP Affinity' and exits 0 (script_rc=0) -> ht_affinity's failures never reach the exit code.

### testcases/kernel/sched/sched_stress/sched_tc6.c  (runtest: sched/sched_stress)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: WEAK, DOCS)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: "a real time process is waiting on a file lock owned by a user process. The scheduler
  should elevate the user process priority to the same level as the real time process".
- Problem: (1) Linux has no priority inheritance for fcntl() locks; the claim is AIX-specific and nothing in
  the code measures it anyway. (2) With -f, fork_realtime() builds the child command from argv[2]/argv[3]
  assuming a fixed positional layout (sched_tc6.c:279-292), but the driver invokes
  `sched_tc6 -tvariable -lsch.measure -pNN -df`, so the child is exec'd as
  `sched_tc6 1 -lsch.measure -pNN 0`: it is NOT "fixed"/real-time (default priority_type "variable"), i.e.
  the scenario the test describes never happens. (3) The child writes its own result with
  fopen(logfile,"w") (sched_tc6.c:204), truncating the parent's line, so sched_driver's measure_test()
  (expects two lines for sched_tc6) gets the child's time as line 1 and an uninitialised t2asc for line 2
  (fgets fails, atof(garbage)). (4) Same time()/100.0 units bug.
- Evidence: sched_tc6.c:26-33, :146, :199-216, :276-305; sched_driver.c:468-473.
- Suggested action: Drop (legacy AIX port whose core claim does not apply to Linux); at minimum fix the
  child argv construction and append instead of truncating the results file.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **REVISED** via RUN,VIRT,READ. VIRT: exec-logging shims over a full sched_stress.sh run: 1620 sched_tc6 execs, all with argv ending '< -d >' or '< -df >' (leading space), and 0 re-execs of the forked child (argv '<1>...'). getopt never sees -f because of the space, so fork_realtime() never runs. Claims (1) and (4) stand. The 'forked child' timing line comes from fgets() on a missing second line.
- Verification conclusion: The finding is right, and the mechanism is worse than phase 1 described. sched_driver passes " -d " and " -df " with a leading space, so getopt treats them as operands. fork_flag stays 0 and fork_realtime() never runs, which means the "real-time process waits on a user process's lock" scenario never happens. The "forked child" result line is computed from a second fgets() on a one-line sch.measure, so it uses an uninitialised buffer. Points (2) and (3) about the child's argv and truncating the log are moot because no child runs. Points (1) (no PI for fcntl locks on Linux) and (4) (time()/100.0) stand. Suggested action: drop.

- Category: WRONG  (secondary: WEAK)

- Claim under test: writing 0 or -1 to /proc/sys/kernel/sched_rt_period_us fails with EINVAL (regression
  test for 079be8fc6309 "Disallow writing invalid values to sched_rt_period_us").
- Problem: `TST_EXP_FAIL(write(period_fd, "0", 2), EINVAL, ...)` (proc_sched_rt01.c:45) writes TWO bytes:
  '0' and the string terminator '\0'. In the kernel, proc_get_long() parses "0", then because
  `len < *size` and the next char '\0' is not in proc_wspace_sep {' ','\t','\n'} it returns -EINVAL
  (kernel/sysctl.c:311-312) before proc_dointvec_minmax ever compares against extra1=SYSCTL_ONE. So the
  "0 -> EINVAL" subcase passes on any kernel, including one without 079be8fc6309 (where 0 would otherwise
  be accepted). The "-1" and "-2" writes are exactly 2 bytes and are fine; the period_us+1 write uses
  strlen() and is fine.
- Evidence: proc_sched_rt01.c:45-46; /usr/src/linux/kernel/sysctl.c:276-320 (proc_get_long),
  :595 (proc_wspace_sep), :699-706; kernel/sched/rt.c:33-41 (extra1 = SYSCTL_ONE).
- Suggested action: use `write(period_fd, "0", 1)` (or strlen) so the range check is what produces EINVAL.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION,VIRT. HPE+VIRT: as-is 5/5 TPASS. Mutant replacing write(period_fd, "0", 2) by write(period_fd, "1000000", 8) (the current valid period plus the trailing NUL) still gives 'TPASS: echo 0 > sched_rt_period_us : EINVAL' on VIRT -> the NUL alone yields EINVAL (proc_get_long), so the 0 subcase cannot detect a kernel lacking 079be8fc6309.

### testcases/kernel/sched/tool/trace_sched.c  (runtest: sched/trace_sched01 `trace_sched -c 1`)
- Category: WRONG  (secondary: WEAK)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: each thread "sets its priority ... reads the priority that the scheduler sets for this
  task and also reads from /proc the processor this task last executed on".
- Problem: (1) The program never compares exp_prio with act_prio; it prints a table and `exit(0)`
  (trace_sched.c:446-462), so it cannot fail. (2) get_proc_num() returns `atoi(&fbuff[fsize - 2])`, the last
  two bytes of /proc/<pid>/stat (trace_sched.c:166-183). Since 2.6 the last field is exit_code
  (fs/proc/array.c:660); the processor is field 39 (fs/proc/array.c:641). So every task is reported on
  "processor 0". (3) The threads call `sched_setscheduler(getpid(), ...)` / `sched_getparam(getpid(), ...)`
  (trace_sched.c:237, :253): on Linux the pid argument is a TID and getpid() is the main thread's TID
  (sched_setscheduler(2) NOTES), so 100 threads race to set the MAIN thread's policy/priority and read it
  back; the threads themselves stay SCHED_OTHER. The collected data therefore describes neither the
  threads nor their CPUs.
- Evidence: trace_sched.c:166-183, :237-262, :446-462; /usr/src/linux/fs/proc/array.c:641,660;
  sched_setscheduler(2) "the thread whose ID is specified in pid".
- Suggested action: Drop (data is meaningless and nothing is asserted), or rewrite with gettid()/
  pthread_setschedparam, parse field 39, and assert act_prio == exp_prio.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,VIRT. HPE (24 CPUs) 'trace_sched -c 24': exit 0; all 2400 rows under 'processor number = 0', 1 distinct 'pid of task' (main PID), and 1953/2400 rows with priority requested != assigned (e.g. requested 37, assigned 22). VIRT 'trace_sched -c 1': 100 rows, 1 PID, 48 mismatches, rc 0. Nothing is asserted.

  deprecation warnings").
- Suggested action: allocate a new ctx for the final aggregate and call EVP_DigestFinal_ex() before freeing.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,VIRT,GIT. ### testcases/kernel/syscalls/accept/accept01.c  (runtest: syscalls/accept01)
- Category: WRONG
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: accept() fails with EINVAL for an "invalid socket buffer" (addr=(struct sockaddr *)3), for an "invalid salen" (addrlen=1) and for "no queued connections".
- Problem: socket_fd is only bound, never listen()ed. All three cases therefore fail in inet_csk_accept() with EINVAL because sk_state != TCP_LISTEN, before the kernel looks at addr or addrlen. The address is only copied out (move_addr_to_user) after ops->accept() succeeds, so the bad-buffer and bad-length cases never run the code they name. "No queued connections" on a blocking listening socket would block, and with O_NONBLOCK it gives EAGAIN, not EINVAL. The three cases are the same test.
- Evidence: accept01.c:47-57,70-71 (no listen); net/socket.c:2059-2071 (ops->accept before getname/move_addr_to_user); net/ipv4/inet_connection_sock.c:662-664 (EINVAL if not TCP_LISTEN). accept(2): "EINVAL Socket is not listening for connections, or addrlen is invalid (e.g., is negative)."
- Suggested action: Keep one "not listening -> EINVAL" case. For the bad-buffer case, use a listening socket with a pending connection and an invalid addr, and expect EFAULT. For the bad-length case, use a negative addrlen on a listening socket with a pending connection (EINVAL from move_addr_to_user). Drop the "no queued connections" case or turn it into a nonblocking EAGAIN case.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION,VIRT. HPE+VIRT: accept01 5/5 TPASS as-is. Mutant with the 'invalid socket buffer' addr (struct sockaddr *)3 replaced by &fsin1 and 'invalid salen' 1 replaced by sizeof(fsin1): still 'TPASS: invalid socket buffer : EINVAL' and 'TPASS: invalid salen : EINVAL' (5/5) -> EINVAL comes from the non-listening socket, not from addr/addrlen.

### testcases/kernel/syscalls/clock_adjtime/clock_adjtime01.c  (runtest: syscalls/clock_adjtime01)
- Category: WRONG
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: clock_adjtime(CLOCK_REALTIME) applies ADJ_OFFSET, ADJ_FREQUENCY, ADJ_MAXERROR, ADJ_ESTERROR, ADJ_TIMECONST and ADJ_TICK. For each, the test reads, adds a delta, sets, and verifies that the value was set.
- Problem: clock_adjtime() copies the whole timex back to user space on success, and __do_adjtimex() overwrites offset/freq/maxerror/esterror/status/constant/tick with the kernel's current state before returning. After the SET call, `ttxc` therefore no longer holds the requested value `val`; it holds whatever the kernel now has. The final check compares that write-back against a second read (`verify`), so it only checks that two consecutive reads agree. If the kernel ignored the requested value, both reads would return the old value and the test would PASS. Also, the nano-resolution detection at line 214 tests `saved.modes & ADJ_NANO`. modes is an input field and stays 0 after a read, so the ADJ_OFFSET scaling for STA_NANO is never applied (cleanup correctly uses STA_NANO). TPASS is also printed after a TFAIL in the same iteration (line 177, missing return).
- Evidence: clock_adjtime01.c:141-177,214; kernel/time/posix-timers.c:1181-1184 (copy_to_user of ktx after do_clock_adjtime); kernel/time/ntp.c:1049-1066 (txc fields overwritten with current state).
- Suggested action: Save `val` before the SET call and compare `timex_get_field_long(&verify, mode)` with `val`. Account for unit conversion: ADJ_OFFSET is only applied with STA_PLL and is the remaining slew, so skip or relax it; freq is in scaled ppm. Detect nano mode via `status & STA_NANO`. Add a `return` after TFAIL.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,MUTATION,VIRT. VIRT: as-is 9/9 TPASS. Mutant setting ttxc.modes=0 right before the SET call (so the kernel applies nothing; SET becomes a pure read) still prints 'TPASS: clock_adjtime(): success' for all 9 modes (8001,a001,403f,1,2,4,8,20,4000) -> the final check only compares two reads.

### testcases/kernel/syscalls/clock_gettime/clock_gettime03.c  (runtest: syscalls/clock_gettime03, containers/clock_gettime03)
- Category: WRONG

So 4 of 6 tcases cannot detect a missing offset in the child, and 2 of 6 cannot detect a failed switch back to the parent ns.

- Suggested action: use llabs(diff - tc->off * 1000) > delta and llabs(diff) > delta.
