### testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigpause/3-1.c  (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigpause/3-1)
- Category: OBSOLETE  (secondary: FRAGILE)
- Confidence: medium
- Claim under test: sigpause() returns -1/EINTR after the handler runs.
- Problem: sigpause was removed in POSIX.1-2024. SIGABRT is not blocked before sigpause, and main only waits sleep(1) before pthread_kill. If the thread has installed the handler but not yet entered sigpause, the signal is consumed early and sigpause blocks forever (HUNG). If it has not installed the handler yet, the process aborts. A sighold() before sigpause (as in 1-1) would close the race.
- Evidence: sigpause/3-1.c:42-43,76-84; XRAT B.1.1.
- Suggested action: drop with the group; if kept, sighold() before sigpause and install the handler before pthread_create.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,MUTATION,READ. As-is PASS; 0 failures in 5 plain + 5 stress runs on HPE and 3 plain + 5 stress runs on VIRT (1 CPU). Mutant with sleep(2) between sigaction() and sigpause() (signal arrives before sigpause, SIGABRT not held) -> sigpause never returns, killed by timeout (rc 137) on HPE and VIRT = HUNG, as phase 1 says; window needs a >1 s delay. glibc 2.43 still provides sigpause; removed in POSIX.1-2024.
- Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): **CONFIRMED** via MUSL,RUN,REPEAT,SRC,READ. HPE ltprepeat 5: glibc pass=5/5, musl pass=5/5 ('returned -1 and set errno to EINTR'); race needs >1 s delay (phase-2 mutant). Issue 8 XRAT 'Removed Functions' lists all 5; both libcs still ship them: glibc 2.43 exports (deprecated attr since 2.32, NEWS:2624), musl exports with no deprecation (include/signal.h:241-246)

### testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigpause/4-1.c  (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigpause/4-1)
- Category: OBSOLETE
- Confidence: low (phase 1: medium)
- Claim under test: sigpause(-1) fails with EINVAL.
- Problem: the logic is fine for Issue 7, but sigpause was removed in POSIX.1-2024. (The `#if 0 && defined(__FreeBSD__) || ...` operator precedence is off but has no effect on Linux.)
- Evidence: sigpause/4-1.c:18,31-48; XRAT B.1.1.
- Suggested action: see the group action.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,BUILD,READ. HPE: sigpause_4-1: Test PASSED: sigpause returned -1 and set errno to EINVAL (rc 0). glibc 2.43 still exports all five (deprecated attr, only -Wdeprecated warnings); XRAT B.1.1 lists them removed in Issue 8. The '#if 0 && ... || defined(__NetBSD__) || ...' precedence slip only affects Net/OpenBSD; none on Linux. Medium: dropping is policy.
- Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): **REVISED** via MUSL,RUN,SRC,READ. HPE glibc: 'sigpause returned -1 and set errno to EINVAL' rc 0; musl: HANGS, killed by 30 s timeout (rc 124). musl bug: src/signal/sigpause.c:7 ignores sigdelset() failure and sigsuspends; glibc sysdeps/posix/sigpause.c:36 returns -1. Issue 7 says 'shall fail' EINVAL. Test still finds libc bugs -> soften drop
- Verification conclusion: This is a musl bug, not a test bug. musl src/signal/sigpause.c:7 ignores the return value of sigdelset(&mask, -1) and calls sigsuspend() on the current mask, so sigpause(-1) blocks forever. glibc sysdeps/posix/sigpause.c:36 returns -1/EINVAL, which is what Issue 7 requires ("shall fail ... illegal signal number"). The interface is still removed in POSIX.1-2024, so OBSOLETE stands. However, this test is the only one in the family that finds a real defect in a shipping libc, so the "drop" action is weaker here: lower to low and suggest "keep while libcs ship sigpause, or drop with the family". The test has no internal alarm and relies on the harness timeout to survive the hang.

### testcases/open_posix_testsuite/stress/threads/pthread_cond_timedwait/stress1.c  (openposix: stress/threads/pthread_cond_timedwait/stress1)
- Category: OBSOLETE  (secondary: FRAGILE, UNDEF)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: pthread_cond_timedwait atomically releases the mutex and blocks. Uses
  ping-pong between thread A and grandchild B (thread or forked process); a 120 s timeout means
  a lost signal.
- Problem: Never built: open_posix stress/threads has no Makefile, so nothing under it is compiled. The test only ends on SIGUSR1, so under t0 it is
  killed and reported HUNG. In the fork scenarios, the child of the multithreaded process calls
  pthread_mutex_lock/cond_timedwait/printf (the output() mutex). POSIX allows only
  async-signal-safe calls after fork() in a multithreaded process, so this is UB. The
  gchild's exit status is read into `ret` and ignored (stress1.c:352). The cleanup
  "destroy the mutex" actually calls pthread_mutex_init(&mtx, &ma) on an initialized mutex
  with an already destroyed attr object, which is UB (stress1.c:672).
- Evidence: stress/Makefile; stress1.c:sighdl/test_main; POSIX fork(): "the child process may
  only execute async-signal-safe operations until such time as one of the exec functions is
  called"; pthread_mutex_init: "Attempting to initialize an already initialized mutex results
  in undefined behavior."
- Suggested action: Drop together with stress/threads, or wire up a Makefile, add a
  self-terminating duration, call pthread_mutex_destroy in cleanup and check the gchild
  exit status.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via BUILD. LTP configure default WITH_OPEN_POSIX_TESTSUITE=no; clean copy + generate-makefiles: no stress/threads/Makefile is generated, so stress/Makefile (*/Makefile only) never descends; make stress-all builds only mqueues+signals (3 tests); no runtest refs; gcc -c -std=c99 compiles OK

### testcases/open_posix_testsuite/stress/threads/pthread_cond_wait/stress1.c  (openposix: stress/threads/pthread_cond_wait/stress1)
- Category: OBSOLETE  (secondary: FRAGILE, UNDEF)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: pthread_cond_wait atomically releases the mutex and blocks. A/B ping-pong;
  if alarm(TIMEOUT=120) fires, a signal was lost.
- Problem: Never built: open_posix stress/threads has no Makefile, so nothing under it is compiled. It does not even compile: test_main does `CD.cid = cid;`
  (stress1.c:582), but this variant's struct childdata has no `cid` member (gcc: "'struct
  childdata' has no member named 'cid'"). It runs until SIGUSR1 (HUNG under t0). Every thread calls
  alarm(TIMEOUT) before each wait, but alarm() is per-process. Any progressing pair re-arms it,
  so a single lost-wakeup pair is not detected until all others stop. The SIGALRM handler calls
  FAILED -> output() (pthread_mutex_lock + printf) and exit(), none of which are
  async-signal-safe. It has the same fork-child UB, ignored gchild status (stress1.c:340) and
  pthread_mutex_init-instead-of-destroy cleanup (stress1.c:669) as the
  pthread_cond_timedwait/stress1.c variant.
- Evidence: stress1.c sighdl (SIGALRM branch); threaded_A/threaded_B `alarm(TIMEOUT)`; POSIX
  alarm(): "alarm requests are not stacked; only one SIGALRM generation can be scheduled".
- Suggested action: Drop, or fix (use pthread_cond_timedwait-based detection, as the
  timedwait variant does) and build it.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via BUILD. LTP configure default WITH_OPEN_POSIX_TESTSUITE=no; clean copy + generate-makefiles: no stress/threads/Makefile is generated, so stress/Makefile (*/Makefile only) never descends; make stress-all builds only mqueues+signals (3 tests); no runtest refs; gcc -c -std=c99: FAIL stress1.c:582 struct childdata has no member cid

### testcases/open_posix_testsuite/stress/threads/pthread_kill/stress.c  (openposix: not selected; would be stress/threads/pthread_kill/stress)
- Category: OBSOLETE  (secondary: WRONG, FRAGILE)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: pthread_kill floods do not destabilise the system, and a signal that is not
  already pending is never lost (SIGILL must be delivered within 5 s).
- Problem: Never built, and it fails to compile with glibc headers: `static int sync;`
  (stress.c:159) redeclares sync(2) from <unistd.h>. The comment "register the signal handler for
  this one thread" is wrong because sigaction() is process-wide. The handlers for
  SIGABRT/SIGBUS/SIGILL are installed inside flood_receiver/sync_rec, which race with the
  already-created flooder_1/flooder_2/sync_send threads. If a sender runs first, the default
  action of SIGABRT/SIGBUS/SIGILL terminates the whole process. The `sync` flag is a plain
  int written from a handler and polled across sleep(), not volatile sig_atomic_t.
- Evidence: gcc 16: "stress.c:159:12: error: 'sync' redeclared as different kind of symbol";
  POSIX sigaction(): the action is per-process; pthread_kill(): "the signal shall be delivered
  to the specified thread" but the action is process-wide.
- Suggested action: Drop, or rename the flag to volatile sig_atomic_t, install the handlers
  in main before creating the senders, and build it.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via BUILD. LTP configure default WITH_OPEN_POSIX_TESTSUITE=no; clean copy + generate-makefiles: no stress/threads/Makefile is generated, so stress/Makefile (*/Makefile only) never descends; make stress-all builds only mqueues+signals (3 tests); no runtest refs; gcc -c -std=c99: FAIL stress.c:159 'sync' redeclared
- Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): **CONFIRMED** via MUSL,BUILD. HPE suite CFLAGS (-std=c99 -D_XOPEN_SOURCE=700): gcc/glibc FAIL stress.c:159 'sync' redeclared; musl-clang FAIL 3 errors: 159 redefinition of 'sync', 163/194 'non-object type void (void) is not assignable'. Unbuildable under both libcs

### testcases/open_posix_testsuite/stress/threads/pthread_mutex_lock/stress.c  (openposix: not selected; would be stress/threads/pthread_mutex_lock/stress)
- Category: OBSOLETE  (secondary: WRONG, UNDEF)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: under heavy signal load (SIGUSR2), lock/timedlock/trylock keep mutual
  exclusion: control() fails if two threads own the mutex simultaneously.
- Problem: Never built (name without digit + no Makefile). The core check is broken:
  control(cell_t *c, char *loc) begins with `*loc++;` (stress.c:204). That increments the
  pointer, not the value. All later `*loc` accesses read and write the byte past the caller's
  `char loc` (stress.c:228/275/332, itself never initialised), which is a stack out-of-bounds
  access. The `*loc = -120` / `*loc = 1` assignments write out of bounds. Because the value is
  garbage and may be 0, `c->ctrl = *loc` can store 0 and the "two threads own the mutex"
  check cannot fire. In addition, SIGUSR1 (the stop request) is process-directed. If it lands
  on a sigthr thread blocked in sem_wait, sem_wait fails with EINTR (the handler is installed with
  sa_flags = 0, no SA_RESTART) and the test reports UNRESOLVED "Sem wait failed".
- Evidence: stress.c:202-218 control(); signal(7): sem_wait(3) is restarted "if the SA_RESTART flag
  was used; otherwise the call fails with the error EINTR"; gcc -Wall: "value computed is not used".
- Suggested action: Drop; if kept, change to `(*loc)++`, initialise loc, retry sem_wait on EINTR.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via BUILD. LTP configure default WITH_OPEN_POSIX_TESTSUITE=no; clean copy + generate-makefiles: no stress/threads/Makefile is generated, so stress/Makefile (*/Makefile only) never descends; make stress-all builds only mqueues+signals (3 tests); no runtest refs; gcc -c -std=c99 compiles OK

### testcases/open_posix_testsuite/stress/threads/pthread_once/stress.c  (openposix: not selected; would be stress/threads/pthread_once/stress)
- Category: OBSOLETE  (secondary: UNDEF)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: init_routine runs exactly once when 30 threads race into pthread_once.
- Problem: Never built (name + missing Makefile), and it runs until SIGUSR1. Each iteration
  re-arms the same once control with `once_ctl = PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT;`.
  PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT is specified only as a static initializer. Resetting a used
  pthread_once_t by assignment is not covered by POSIX. It works with glibc's int-based
  pthread_once_t only.
- Evidence: stress.c test_main loop; POSIX pthread_once: "The behavior of pthread_once() is
  undefined if once_control has automatic storage duration or is not initialized by
  PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT."
- Suggested action: Drop, or use a fresh static pthread_once_t per iteration (e.g. an array).
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via BUILD. LTP configure default WITH_OPEN_POSIX_TESTSUITE=no; clean copy + generate-makefiles: no stress/threads/Makefile is generated, so stress/Makefile (*/Makefile only) never descends; make stress-all builds only mqueues+signals (3 tests); no runtest refs; gcc -c -std=c99 compiles OK
- Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): **REVISED** via MUSL,BUILD,RUN,SRC. HPE built under both; SIGUSR1 after 10s: glibc 'PASSED -- 7728 iterations', musl 'PASSED -- 7368 iterations'. 'Works with glibc's int-based once only' is wrong: musl pthread_once_t is int, INIT 0 (alltypes.h.in:58, pthread.h:61, pthread_once.c:19 states 0-3); reset after join works on both. Only formal POSIX UB remains
- Verification conclusion: OBSOLETE (never built, runs until SIGUSR1) stands. The secondary claim, "works with glibc's int-based pthread_once_t only", is wrong. musl's pthread_once_t is also an int with PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT 0 (include/alltypes.h.in:58, pthread.h:61). Its state machine (0/1/2/3, src/thread/pthread_once.c:19-36) is reset correctly by assignment once all threads are joined, and glibc behaves the same (sysdeps/nptl/bits/pthreadtypes.h:53). Corrected secondary text: "re-arming by assignment is formally undefined in POSIX, but harmless on glibc and musl." The action (drop) is unchanged.

#### Grouped entries (OBSOLETE)

### sighold / sigignore / sigpause / sigrelse / sigset directories (shared evidence for the OBSOLETE entries below)
POSIX.1-2024 (Issue 8) removed these XSI functions: https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/xrat/V4_xsh_chap01.html
B.1.1 "Removed Functions in Issue 8" lists sighold, sigignore, sigpause, sigrelse and sigset, and
https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/sighold.html returns 404. sigset(3) HISTORY says
"POSIX.1-2008 marks these functions as obsolete"; sigpause(3) says "Obsoleted in POSIX.1-2008". glibc still provides them, marked
deprecated. The tests are judged against Issue 7 text, which still applies to them; where a test also has a logic
problem, its own section says so. Suggested action for the whole group: decide once whether open_posix keeps
Issue 7-only coverage. If it does not, drop these directories (or move them to a "removed interfaces" area that is not run by default).

### testcases/commands/tpm-tools/ (whole suite, runtest/tpm_tools: tpm01-tpm07, tpmtoken01-05)
- Category: OBSOLETE  (secondary: FRAGILE)
- Confidence: medium
- Claim under test: TrouSerS tpm-tools (tpm_version, tpm_selftest, tpm_getpubek, tpm_takeownership, tpm_restrictpubek, tpm_changeownerauth, tpm_clear) and the opencryptoki PKCS#11 tpmtoken_* tools work against the TPM.
- Problem: All 12 scripts (plus 28 expect helpers *_exp0N.sh) target TPM 1.2 userspace (tcsd/TrouSerS, tpm-tools), unchanged since 2005-2009 (git log only shows license/address edits). They test userspace tools, not the kernel (only /dev/tpm0 underneath). None detects a TPM or its version: on systems with no TPM or a TPM 2.0 (practically all current hardware) they TBROK (tool missing) or TFAIL (tcsd cannot talk to a TPM 2.0), never TCONF. The runtest order forms one stateful sequence (getpubek needs an un-owned TPM, takeownership takes ownership with fixed passwords, restrictpubek permanently restricts PUBEK, changeauth chains passwords across subtests, tpmtoken_init test01 fails if the token is already initialized, tpm_clear clears ownership which on TPM 1.2 leaves it disabled until reboot), so it can run once on a freshly cleared TPM 1.2 and cannot be re-run. Each expect helper waits a full 30 s `expect timeout` in the hang case and the pass/fail is only the tool exit code. They use the legacy apicmds (tst_resm/tst_brk binaries) API.
- Evidence: runtest/tpm_tools; e.g. testcases/commands/tpm-tools/tpm/tpm_getpubek/tpm_getpubek_tests.sh:46-55 (only `which` check, TBROK); tpm_restrictpubek_tests_exp01.sh:25 (`tpm_restrictpubek -r`); tpm_clear_tests_exp01.sh:25; tpmtoken_init_tests_exp01.sh:37-55 (fails if store already initialized).
- Suggested action: drop runtest/tpm_tools and testcases/commands/tpm-tools/ (kernel TPM coverage is better served by IMA/tpm2 based tests); if kept, add TPM 1.2 presence detection with TCONF and document that it is destructive.

All *_exp0N.sh files are expect helpers of these scripts and go with them.

### testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/definitions/signal_h/17-1-buildonly.c, 18-1-buildonly.c  (openposix: conformance/definitions/signal_h/17-1-buildonly, 18-1-buildonly)
- Category: OBSOLETE  (18-1 secondary: WEAK)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: "ucontext.h shall define ucontext_t" (17) / "... mcontext_t" (18).
- Problem: <ucontext.h> (getcontext/makecontext/swapcontext) was removed from POSIX in Issue 7;
  ucontext_t and mcontext_t are now defined by <signal.h> (CX). Additionally 18-1 is a
  byte-for-byte copy of 17-1 and never references mcontext_t.
- Evidence: signal_h/17-1, 18-1 (both `#include <ucontext.h>` + `static ucontext_t dummy;`);
  signal.h.html: "shall define the mcontext_t type through typedef", "shall define the
  ucontext_t type as a structure".
- Suggested action: switch to `#include <signal.h>` and make 18-1 use mcontext_t.

### testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/definitions/signal_h/{2-3,21-1,22-30..22-35,35-1,36-1,37-1,40-1,44-1,45-1}-buildonly.c  (openposix: conformance/definitions/signal_h/*)
- Category: OBSOLETE
- Confidence: high (21-1: medium, only the si_band part is affected)
- Claim under test: <signal.h> defines SIG_HOLD (2-3), siginfo_t.si_band (21-1), POLL_IN/OUT/MSG/
  ERR/PRI/HUP (22-30..22-35), and declares sighold (35), sigignore (36), siginterrupt (37),
  sigpause (40), sigrelse (44), sigset (45).
- Problem: All of these were obsolescent in POSIX.1-2008 (XSI STREAMS / old signal API) and were
  removed in POSIX.1-2024 by Austin Group Defect 1330. The current <signal.h> lists neither
  SIG_HOLD, si_band, the POLL_* codes, nor these functions. The tests still pass on glibc
  (which keeps them, partly marked deprecated), but they assert requirements that no longer
  exist; a conforming Issue 8 libc may omit them and get a "compile FAILED".
- Evidence: https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/basedefs/signal.h.html (prototype list
  has no sighold/sigignore/siginterrupt/sigpause/sigrelse/sigset; only SIG_DFL/SIG_ERR/SIG_IGN;
  siginfo_t has no si_band; CHANGE HISTORY Issue 8: "Austin Group Defect 1330 is applied,
  removing obsolescent interfaces.")
- Suggested action: drop these buildonly tests (for 21-1 drop only the si_band line).

### testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/definitions/time_h/9-1-buildonly.c, 17-1-buildonly.c  (openposix: conformance/definitions/time_h/9-1-buildonly, 17-1-buildonly)
- Category: OBSOLETE
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: <time.h> declares asctime_r() (9-1) and ctime_r() (17-1).
- Problem: Both functions were obsolescent in POSIX.1-2008 and removed in POSIX.1-2024. glibc

- Evidence: https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/basedefs/time.h.html CHANGE HISTORY
  Issue 8: "Austin Group Defect 1410 is applied, removing the asctime_r() and ctime_r() functions."
- Suggested action: drop both.

### v4l user_space test_VIDIOC_*.c files: common problems

All remaining files in this directory (test_VIDIOC_AUDIO .. test_VIDIOC_EXT_CTRLS) are part of
the 2009 "v4l-test" CUnit suite by Marton Nemeth imported into LTP. Common to all of them:
- Not built by LTP: v4l/ is not in testcases/kernel/device-drivers/Makefile SUBDIRS, the
  stand-alone v4l/user_space/Makefile links `-lcunit` and is unaware of LTP's build system;
  there is no runtest entry and no LTP result reporting (CUnit asserts only). git log shows
  only whitespace/style churn since import.
- They encode the pre-3.1 V4L2 convention that an unimplemented ioctl returns EINVAL.
  Since v3.1 (commit 9190d191b1b8 "[media] v4l2 core: return -ENOTTY if an ioctl doesn't
  exist") the core returns ENOTTY: drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c:3078,3117-3119
  (`ret = -ENOTTY; if (!is_valid_ioctl(vfd, cmd) ...) goto done;`), documented in
  Documentation/userspace-api/media/gen-errors.rst:60 "ENOTTY  The ioctl is not supported by
  the file descriptor." Every "not supported" branch (`CU_ASSERT_EQUAL(errno_x, EINVAL)`)
  therefore fails on any device that lacks the ioctl (e.g. uvcvideo webcams lack audio,
  tuner, std and crop ioctls).
- The *_NULL subtests require "ioctl not supported => NULL argument gives EINVAL". The core
  copies the argument in before dispatch for _IOW/_IOWR ioctls (video_usercopy ->
  video_get_user, v4l2-ioctl.c:3437-3451, 3302-3304), so NULL yields EFAULT for them, and
  ENOTTY for _IOR ones; EINVAL is never the result.
- Suggested action for all: drop testcases/kernel/device-drivers/v4l (and the usb tree).
  v4l2-compliance from v4l-utils is the maintained conformance suite and is used upstream
  with vivid/vimc in CI; if LTP wants V4L2 coverage it should be a new tst_test-based test
  on vivid.
Per-file specifics follow.


## DOCS: Inaccurate description, comments or metadata

The test logic is sound but what it says about itself (header comment, docparse block, runtest entry) is wrong or misleading. Action: fix the text only.

69 testcases. Sorted by path; confidence shown in each entry.

### testcases/cve/sctphantom.c  (runtest: cve/cve-2026-64564)
- Category: DOCS  (secondary: FRAGILE)
- Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
- Claim under test: CVE-2026-64564 SCTP ASCONF DEL-IP UAF; fixed kernel answers the first DEL-IP with SCTP_ERROR_REQ_REFUSED (matches fix 9b2854f86f0b, net/sctp/sm_make_chunk.c sctp_process_asconf_param()).
- Problem: The docparse says the sysctls exist only while the sctp module is loaded "so the test reports TCONF if it is not (run modprobe sctp first)". The code instead calls tst_modprobe("sctp", NULL) unconditionally in setup, which runs tst_cmd(..., flags 0): any non-zero modprobe exit or a missing modprobe binary is TBROK (lib/tst_cmd.c:104-112), e.g. CONFIG_IP_SCTP=y on a system without /lib/modules/$(uname -r) or without kmod. The doc text is wrong and the environment case gives TBROK instead of TCONF.
- Evidence: testcases/cve/sctphantom.c:45-49 vs :208; lib/tst_module.c:150-169; lib/tst_cmd.c:65-66,111-112.
- Suggested action: use `.needs_drivers = {"sctp", NULL}` (handles built-in and loads modules) or pass TST_CMD_TCONF_ON_MISSING and tolerate failure; fix the doc paragraph accordingly.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **REVISED** via RUN,READ. HPE, sctp not loaded: no modprobe in PATH -> tst_cmd returns 255 silently, then 'tst_sys_conf.c:73: TCONF: Path not found: /proc/sys/net/sctp/addip_enable'. modprobe present but failing (-d empty dir, as without kernel-modules-extra) -> 'tst_cmd.c:112: TBROK: modprobe exited with a non-zero code 1' + CVE 'may be vulnerable' hints. Doc wrong; missing binary gives TCONF, not TBROK
- Verification conclusion: The doc paragraph is wrong: setup() modprobes sctp itself (sysctls are saved only after that), so "run modprobe sctp first" is not needed. When modprobe runs and fails (e.g. Fedora without kernel-modules-extra) the result is TBROK with a misleading "may be vulnerable" hint. Phase 1 was wrong on one detail: a *missing* modprobe binary is silently ignored by tst_cmd() (returns 255) and ends in TCONF from the sysctl save. Suggested fix stands (.needs_drivers sctp, fix the doc). The exploit part was not run (not needed for a DOCS finding).

  ns); after setsid() both are 1".

HPE: pidns02 TPASS getsid(0)==0, getpgid(0)==0, then after setsid() getsid(0)==1, getpgid(0)==1 (all child-side); doc still says 'parent process group ID must be 1' and omits the pre-setsid 0 checks; wording inherited from 2007 version, 3fc912172c32 only fixed a flag name

- Category: DOCS

Mutation: thread 0 ftruncate(fd,0) before its memset -> SIGBUS, handler returns, fault repeats; no 'Unexpected signal caught' TFAIL ever printed, result 'TBROK: Test killed! (timeout?)' after the full runtime. Header: '(maximum 1GB)' vs code (1+rand%1000)*4096 <= ~4 MB confirmed by reading

### testcases/kernel/sched/cfs-scheduler/starvation.c  (runtest: sched/starvation)
- Category: DOCS  (secondary: FRAGILE, UNDEF)
- Confidence: high

- Problem: (1) Option help text is wrong: "-l Number of loops (default 2000000)" but `loop = 1000000`; "-t Max timeout (default 240s)" but the default is a calibrated value (`callibrate()/1000`, i.e. the microseconds for 120M empty loops reinterpreted as seconds). (2) The TFAIL criterion is "took longer than the calibrated runtime", a wall-clock budget derived from an empty-loop calibration; on noisy VMs/steal time it can mis-fire, though the margin is usually large (low confidence). (3) `loop` is a plain `static long` decremented in the signal handler and polled by `while (loop) sleep(1);`; strictly UB per C (needs `volatile sig_atomic_t`), in practice the call to sleep() forces a reload.
- Evidence: starvation.c:27, 31-54, 111-112, 120-124, 148-156, 166-167.
- Suggested action: fix the option help strings (and document how the default runtime is derived); make `loop` volatile.

### testcases/kernel/syscalls/modify_ldt/modify_ldt01.c  (runtest: syscalls/modify_ldt01)
- Category: DOCS  (secondary: FRAGILE)
- Confidence: medium
- Claim under test: "Fails with EINVAL, when writing (func=1) to an invalid pointer".
- Problem: That case is {1, NULL, 0, EINVAL}. write_ldt() returns EINVAL because
  bytecount (0) != sizeof(struct user_desc), before it reads the pointer. A NULL pointer with
  the correct bytecount gives EFAULT. So this case checks the same condition as the next one
  (bytecount sizeof-1), and the description is wrong. Separately, the EFAULT case uses
  sbrk(0)+0xFFF as the "invalid" address. That address becomes valid if anything grows the
  heap with brk() after setup (glibc malloc from library or stdio code); tst_get_bad_addr()
  is the reliable choice. The {0, &buf, sizeof(buf)} case reads into the pointer variable
  `buf`, not the guarded buffer, which also looks unintended.
- Evidence: modify_ldt01.c:13, 33-36, 61; arch/x86/kernel/ldt.c write_ldt(): `error =
  -EINVAL; if (bytecount != sizeof(ldt_info)) goto out; error = -EFAULT; if
  (copy_from_user(...))`.
- Suggested action: reword it as "invalid bytecount (0)", or add a real
  NULL-pointer/correct-size case that expects EFAULT. Use tst_get_bad_addr() for the read
  EFAULT case.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,VIRT,READ. VIRT: 'TCONF: This arch x86_64 is not supported' (test is #ifdef __i386__ only, so it runs nowhere in this lab). arch/x86/kernel/ldt.c write_ldt(): 'error = -EINVAL; if (bytecount != sizeof(ldt_info)) goto out;' precedes copy_from_user -> {1, NULL, 0} is a bytecount check, not an invalid-pointer check; docs wrong. sbrk(0)+0xFFF EFAULT fragility holds by reading.
- Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): **UNCHANGED** via MUSL,RUN. HPE glibc and musl: 'TCONF: This arch x86_64 is not supported for test!' (i386-only). Kernel write_ldt() ordering argument is libc-independent

### testcases/kernel/syscalls/recvfrom/recvfrom01.c  (runtest: syscalls/recvfrom01)
- Category: DOCS
- Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
- Claim under test: recvfrom() returns the proper errno for various failure cases.
- Problem: Test case 3 is described as "invalid socket buffer" with experrno ENOTSOCK, but its retval is 0, so it requires recvfrom() with `src_addr=(void*)-1` on a connected TCP socket to SUCCEED. That holds because TCP does not report a source address (msg_namelen stays 0 and nothing is copied), but the case name and ENOTSOCK are misleading. Cases 6/7 call MSG_OOB/MSG_ERRQUEUE "invalid flags", but they are valid flags that fail because there is no urgent data or the error queue is empty. recv01 and recvmsg01 have the same wording.
- Evidence: recvfrom01.c:97-101 (retval 0, ENOTSOCK), :135-151 (only checks errno if retval<0); net/socket.c __sys_recvfrom only calls move_addr_to_user with msg_namelen (0 for TCP).
- Suggested action: Rename case 3 to "connected TCP ignores invalid src_addr" with experrno 0, and reword the MSG_OOB/MSG_ERRQUEUE descriptions.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,READ,VIRT. VIRT as-is 7 TPASS incl. 'invalid socket buffer successful': case 3 has retval 0 (src_addr=(void*)-1 on connected TCP succeeds), so its ENOTSOCK and name are unused/misleading; cases 6/7 'invalid MSG_OOB/MSG_ERRQUEUE flag' get EINVAL/EAGAIN from empty urgent data / error queue, not invalid flags

### testcases/kernel/syscalls/request_key/request_key02.c  (runtest: syscalls/request_key02)
- Category: DOCS (phase 1: WRONG)
- Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
- Claim under test: request_key() fails with EKEYREVOKED when "a revoked key was found" and EKEYEXPIRED when "an expired key was found" (request_key(2) ERRORS).
- Problem: For the revoked and expired cases, the test passes the revoked/expired key's own serial as the `dest_keyring` argument (`request_key("keyring", "ltp2", NULL, key2)`). The syscall validates the destination keyring with lookup_user_key(..., KEY_LOOKUP_CREATE, KEY_NEED_WRITE) before any search, and key_validate() returns -EKEYREVOKED / -EKEYEXPIRED for that destination. The errno therefore comes from "invalid destination keyring", and the documented search-path behaviour is never reached. A kernel whose search returned the wrong errno for a revoked or expired match would still pass.
- Evidence: request_key02.c verify_request_key() (dest = *tc->id) and setup(); security/keys/keyctl.c:203-212 (dest lookup before key_type_lookup/request_key_and_link); security/keys/permission.c:102-119 (key_validate); request_key(2): "EKEYREVOKED A revoked key was found, but no replacement could be obtained."
- Suggested action: Pass dest_keyring 0 (or KEY_SPEC_THREAD_KEYRING) for all cases so the error comes from the search. Optionally keep the revoked-destination case as a separate, correctly described subcase.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **REVISED** via RUN,MUTATION,READ,VIRT. VIRT as-is 3 TPASS. Mutant searching nonexistent descriptions with dest=revoked/expired key still gets EKEYREVOKED/EKEYEXPIRED -> errno from dest validation (confirmed). But mutant with dest=0 gets ENOKEY for both: request_key search skips expired keys (SKIP_EXPIRED) and ranks EKEYREVOKED below EAGAIN, so the suggested 'dest 0' fix would TFAIL on a correct kernel
- Verification conclusion: Phase 1 is right that the errno comes from validating the destination keyring (mutant A), not from the search. Its suggested fix is wrong, though: on 7.2 the search path returns ENOKEY. request_key's search uses KEYRING_SEARCH_SKIP_EXPIRED (request_key.c:593), and search_cred_keyrings_rcu ranks EKEYREVOKED below the EAGAIN from the other keyrings (process_keys.c:433), so request_key then reports ENOKEY. Corrected finding: the subcases really test "dest_keyring is revoked/expired", which is valid kernel behaviour with a misleading description. Corrected action: rename them as such and keep the dest argument. Do not switch to dest 0. Optionally add a search case expecting ENOKEY.

### testcases/kernel/syscalls/socket/socket01.c  (runtest: syscalls/socket01)
- Category: DOCS
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: "EPROTONOSUPPORT on raw open as non-root".
- Problem: The test does not drop privileges (no setuid, no .needs_root=0 enforcement) and the
  case uses socket(PF_INET, SOCK_RAW, 0). EPROTONOSUPPORT here comes from protocol 0 being
  rejected for SOCK_RAW in inet_create()'s protosw lookup, which runs before the CAP_NET_RAW
  check. The result is the same for root and non-root, so the label is misleading. A real non-root
  raw socket attempt (with a valid protocol) gives EPERM.
- Evidence: socket01.c:15,40; net/ipv4/af_inet.c inet_create(): lookup loop sets
  err=-EPROTONOSUPPORT (func+37) before `err = -EPERM` / CAP_NET_RAW check (func+62..64).
- Suggested action: reword to "EPROTONOSUPPORT on SOCK_RAW with protocol 0" (optionally add a
  real non-root EPERM case with IPPROTO_ICMP after dropping privileges).

### testcases/kernel/sysfs/class/bdi/sys_bdi01.c  (runtest: sysfs/sys_bdi01)
- Category: DOCS
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: min_bytes <= max_bytes "when max_bytes is set (0 means no limit)".
- Problem: max_bytes is not an independent "limit set" value; it is computed on every read from max_ratio and the current global dirty threshold, so it is non-zero whenever max_ratio > 0 (default 100%). The "0 means no limit" wording is wrong; the check itself is harmless (min_ratio <= max_ratio is enforced, so min_bytes <= max_bytes for one threshold value).
- Evidence: test lines 15-16, 53-59; /usr/src/linux/mm/page-writeback.c:661-671 bdi_get_bytes(), :766-769 bdi_get_max_bytes(); mm/backing-dev.c:393-400 max_bytes_show().
- Suggested action: reword the description (max_bytes reflects max_ratio scaled by the current dirty threshold); the max_bytes > 0 guard can stay.

### testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigwait/1-1.c  (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigwait/1-1)
- Category: DOCS
- Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
- Claim under test: the header says "If no signal in 'set' is pending at the time of the call, the thread shall be suspended until one or more becomes pending". Steps: block, call sigwait(), raise, verify return.
- Problem: the code raises SIGUSR2 and checks that it is pending before calling sigwait(), so it tests the "signal already pending" path (selection + clearing from the pending set), not suspension. The closing comment "the process was suspended until SIGUSR2 was raised" is false. The suspension assertion is actually tested by sigwait/4-1.c. The logic itself is valid.
- Evidence: sigwait/1-1.c:8-14 vs 43-63,81-82.
- Suggested action: reword the header to describe the pending-signal path, or merge with 8-1.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,READ,GIT. HPE PASS. Code raise()s SIGUSR2 and asserts it is pending (l.48-62) before sigwait(), so only the already-pending path is exercised; suspension is covered by sigwait/4-1 (alarm(3) then sigwait). Header text unchanged since 2002 import. Also l.82 message 'is not pending!' should read 'still pending'.

- Suggested action: reword header to "two overruns" / sleep of VALUESEC + 2*INTERVALSEC + 1.

### testcases/open_posix_testsuite/functional/timers/timers/twoevtimers.c  (openposix: functional/timers/timers/twoevtimers)
- Category: DOCS  (secondary: FRAGILE)
- Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
- Claim under test: header: "two timers in different processes set to expire at the same time".
- Problem: The code creates both timers (SIGABRT, SIGALRM) in a single process, so the header
  is wrong (copied from twoptimers.c). Also sleep(EXPIREDELTA + 1) returns as soon as the first
  handler runs, so the check relies on the second signal already being pending at that point.
  On Linux both hrtimers with identical expiry fire in the same interrupt, so this normally
  holds, but it is not guaranteed. Counters are plain int, not volatile sig_atomic_t.
- Evidence: twoevtimers.c header comment vs test_main; `sleep(EXPIREDELTA + 1);` followed by
  immediate check.
- Suggested action: fix the description; loop on sleep/sigsuspend until both counters are set
  or a deadline passes.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **CONFIRMED** via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,READ. Header says 'two timers in different processes'; the code arms SIGABRT+SIGALRM timers in one process. All runs PASS (HPE 11/11 incl. 5 under stress, VIRT 6/6), so the secondary FRAGILE note (sleep returns after the first handler) was not reproduced. An untracked /usr/src/ltp/.../twoevtimers.c~ already holds a reworded header.


## Refuted in verification (now OK)

Phase-1 findings that phase 2 or phase 3 showed to be wrong: the test's check does fail when it should, or the claimed problem does not occur. Kept here for transparency; no action needed.

### testcases/kernel/security/smack/smack_set_socket_labels.c  (runtest: smack/smack_set_socket_labels)
- Category: OK (phase 1: WRONG)
- Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
- Claim under test: fsetxattr() of security.SMACK64IPIN/IPOUT on a UDP socket succeeds, unknown SMACK64IPNOT is rejected; TCONF when Smack is not active.
- Problem: `char buf[256]` is never initialised and the return value of `flistxattr(sock, buf, 256)` is ignored (line 82). When Smack is not enabled, vfs_listxattr() on a sockfs inode writes nothing (sockfs has no ->listxattr, only security_inode_listsecurity contributes), so `strstr(buf, ...)` on line 83 reads stack garbage (UB) and the TCONF/continue decision is random. Even with Smack active, strstr only inspects the first NUL-terminated name in the list, so the check works by accident of ordering.
- Evidence: test lines 76-84; /usr/src/linux/fs/xattr.c vfs_listxattr() (no i_op->listxattr for sockfs -> only LSM names); the actual assertions (lines 86-103) are correct per security/smack/smack_lsm.c smack_inode_setsecurity() which accepts only SMACK64/SMACK64IPIN/SMACK64IPOUT for sockets.
- Suggested action: check flistxattr() return value (<=0 -> TCONF) and scan the returned list properly (iterate NUL-separated names up to the returned length); zero the buffer.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **REFUTED** via RUN,VIRT,READ. VIRT: flistxattr() on a UDP socket with buf prefilled 0xAA returns 38 '[security.selinux] [system.sockprotoname]': sockfs HAS ->listxattr (net/socket.c:646,693 sockfs_listxattr -> simple_xattr_list -> security_inode_listsecurity), so buf is always filled; Smack lists security.SMACK64 first. TCONF decision is deterministic; test TCONFs as-is.
- Verification conclusion: Phase 1's premise is wrong: sockfs does implement ->listxattr (net/socket.c:646 and :693, sockfs_listxattr -> simple_xattr_list -> security_inode_listsecurity, then always appends "system.sockprotoname"), so flistxattr() always fills buf. With Smack active, security.SMACK64 is the first name, and Smack and SELinux are exclusive, so the strstr() TCONF decision is deterministic. The unchecked return value and first-name-only strstr() are hygiene issues, not a test defect. Suggested report text: OK. Optional cleanup: check the flistxattr() return value.

### testcases/kernel/syscalls/shmget/shmget05.c  (runtest: syscalls/shmget05)
- Category: OK (phase 1: WRONG)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: writing N to /proc/sys/kernel/shm_next_id makes the next shmget() return id N
  and resets shm_next_id to -1.
- Problem: verify_shmget() removes the segment (SAFE_SHMCTL(shm_id, IPC_RMID), line 40) but
  leaves shm_id set to the stale id. cleanup() then calls SAFE_SHMCTL(shm_id, IPC_RMID) again
  (lines 52-53) because shm_id != -1; the kernel returns EINVAL for the removed id, and
  tst_brk in cleanup is converted to TWARN (lib/tst_test.c:408-418), so the test ends with a
  warning / non-zero exit on every run on a correct kernel. (Also shm_id is statically 0, not
  -1, so the guard is wrong even before the first iteration.)
- Evidence: shmget05.c:26,40,52-53; lib/tst_safe_sysv_ipc.c:197-201; lib/tst_test.c:408-425.
- Suggested action: set shm_id = -1 after IPC_RMID in verify_shmget() and initialise it to -1.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **REFUTED** via RUN,MUTATION,READ. HPE: shmget05 TPASS, warnings 0 (also -i 3). Instrumented cleanup prints shm_id=-1: SAFE_SHMCTL macro sets its id arg to -1 on IPC_RMID (include/tst_safe_sysv_ipc.h:50-53), so no double RMID. Only nit: static 0 init means early tst_brk before shmget would RMID id 0
- Verification conclusion: Phase 1 missed that SAFE_SHMCTL is a macro that assigns -1 to its shmid argument when cmd == IPC_RMID (include/tst_safe_sysv_ipc.h:50-53), so cleanup never repeats the RMID and no TWARN is produced. The only remaining nit (not worth a finding) is the static 0 initialisation: if SAFE_FILE_PRINTF breaks before the first shmget, cleanup does shmctl(0, IPC_RMID). Entry should be dropped / marked OK.

### testcases/kernel/syscalls/shmget/shmget06.c  (runtest: syscalls/shmget06)
- Category: OK (phase 1: WRONG)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: when shm_next_id names an id already in use, shmget() returns a different id.
- Problem: verify_shmget() removes shm_id[1] (line 39) without resetting it; cleanup() loops
  over shm_id[0..1] and SAFE_SHMCTL(shm_id[1], IPC_RMID) fails with EINVAL on the stale id,
  which tst_test converts into TWARN on every run. shm_id[] is also zero-initialised, so the
  `!= -1` guard does not protect the not-yet-created case either.
- Evidence: shmget06.c:24,39,55-58; lib/tst_test.c:408-425.
- Suggested action: set shm_id[1] = -1 after IPC_RMID; initialise both ids to -1.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **REFUTED** via RUN,READ. HPE: shmget06 TPASS, warnings 0. Same as shmget05: SAFE_SHMCTL(shm_id[1], IPC_RMID) resets shm_id[1] to -1 (tst_safe_sysv_ipc.h:52), cleanup only removes shm_id[0]. Nit: zero-init ids only matter if setup breaks before shmget
- Verification conclusion: Same as shmget05 (verified by instrumentation there): SAFE_SHMCTL(shm_id[1], IPC_RMID) resets shm_id[1] to -1, so cleanup only removes shm_id[0]; no TWARN on any run. Only nit: zero-initialised ids would matter only if setup broke before SAFE_SHMGET. Mark OK.

### testcases/network/stress/route/route-change-netlink-dst.sh  (runtest: net_stress.route route4-change-netlink-dst, route6-change-netlink-dst)
- Category: OK (phase 1: WRONG)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: add/delete routes to several destinations via netlink (route-change-netlink binary).
- Problem: setup builds `ROUTE_CHANGE_NETLINK_PARAMS="-d $(tst_iface) -r '$rhost_all'"`; route-lib.sh test_netlink runs `$cmd $opt` without eval, so word splitting passes the single quotes literally: `-r "'10.23.4.1,...,10.23.0.1,'"`. strtok on ',' yields "'10.23.4.1" and "'" which SAFE_GETADDRINFO cannot resolve -> TBROK in setup -> exit 2 -> test_netlink reports TFAIL. With libmnl present the test cannot pass; without libmnl it TCONFs, which likely hid the bug. Present since the test was added (553ca8ea3bc5).
- Evidence: route-change-netlink-dst.sh:32; route-lib.sh:93,98 (`$cmd $opt`); route-change-netlink.c:74,123 (SAFE_GETADDRINFO on each item). Verified: `opt="-r '1.2.3.4,5.6.7.8,'"; printf '<%s>\n' $opt` prints `<'1.2.3.4,5.6.7.8,'>`; getaddrinfo("'1.2.3.4") -> EAI_NONAME.
- Suggested action: drop the inner single quotes (the list has no spaces), or use `eval` in test_netlink.
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **REFUTED** via RUN,READ. HPE: route-change-netlink-dst.sh and -6 both TPASS ('routes created and deleted', 10000 loops) with the literal quotes in argv (-r '10.23.4.1,...,'). Reason: strtok delim is TST_TO_STR(IP_ADDR_DELIM) where IP_ADDR_DELIM is ',' -> string "','", so the quote char is also a delimiter and gets stripped.
- Verification conclusion: The literal single quotes do reach argv, but route-change-netlink.c splits with `strtok(item, TST_TO_STR(IP_ADDR_DELIM))` where `#define IP_ADDR_DELIM ','`; stringifying the char literal yields the string `"','"`, so `'` is itself a delimiter and the quotes are discarded. The test works (by accident). At most a cosmetic note: drop the inner quotes / define the delimiter as a string. No functional finding.

### testcases/network/stress/route/route-change-netlink-if.sh  (runtest: net_stress.route route4-change-netlink-if, route6-change-netlink-if)
- Category: OK (phase 1: WRONG)
- Confidence: high
- Claim under test: switch route output interface via netlink across several ifaces/gateways.
- Problem: same quoting bug as -dst: `ROUTE_CHANGE_NETLINK_PARAMS="-d '$iface_all' -g '$gw_all' -r $rhost"` passes literal quotes; save_iface() calls if_nametoindex("'ltp_ns_veth...") -> fails -> tst_brk(TBROK) -> shell reports TFAIL. The test can never pass when built with libmnl.
- Evidence: route-change-netlink-if.sh:35; route-lib.sh:98; route-change-netlink.c:59-61,122.
- Suggested action: remove the single quotes (or eval in test_netlink).
- Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): **REFUTED** via RUN,READ. HPE: route-change-netlink-if.sh TPASS as-is (also -gw TPASS). Same reason as -dst: route-change-netlink.c strtok delimiter TST_TO_STR(',') expands to the 3-char string "','" so literal single quotes from -d '...' -g '...' are treated as delimiters.
- Verification conclusion: Same as -dst: the `'` characters around the -d/-g lists are consumed as strtok delimiters (TST_TO_STR(',') == "','"), so if_nametoindex() gets clean names. Test passes on 7.2.
